title: Arsenal weigh up Kounde move to ease defensive issues
description: Arsenal are contemplating an approach to sign Jules Kounde from Barcelona to ease the club’s defensive concerns.With William Saliba sidelined for an extended period and Jurrien Timber being eased ba...
fullText:
Arsenal are contemplating an approach to sign Jules Kounde from Barcelona to ease the club's defensive concerns.

With William Saliba sidelined for an extended period and Jurrien Timber being eased back into action after injury, Arsenal want to sign a player who can play at centre-back and right-back, with Kounde fitting that profile.

The Premier League champions have discussed a deal for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, though Kounde has now emerged as an alternative, according to Spanish outlet SPORT.

Mikel Arteta is a 'big admirer' of the France international, though Kounde's agent has denied that he held talks with Barcelona officials this week to discuss a potential move.

The 27-year-old renewed his contract until 2030 just a year ago, and remains committed to the La Liga champions. Arsenal are not alone in expressing interest in Kounde, with Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich both linked of late.

After Wednesday's draw with Como, Arsenal manager Mikel Areta outlined his desire for more signings.

"There is more that we want to do because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that," Arteta said.

"We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.

"But the approach, the will and the desire of the club, that's unquestionable. We want to try to do that. But we cannot promise that we're going to do it because it doesn't only depend on us."

title: What signing Hassan Haskins, JaMycal Hasty means for the Patriots
description: The Patriots made some changes at running back on Wednesday.
fullText:
Before kicking off their 2026 preseason on Thursday night, the New England Patriots made some changes to their running back group. Besides putting undrafted rookie Myles Montgomery on the waiver wire, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel also signed veteran free agents Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty.

Let's assess what the moves mean for New England with the Colts game on the horizon.

Haskins and Hasty are quite similar considering that both have several years of NFL experience on their résumé and are able to fill more than one roles for the team.

Haskins, a 2022 fourth-round draft pick, has played a combined 46 regular season and playoff games over the course of his career. A big-bodied back at 6-foot-2, 228 pounds, he is not your classic between-the-tackles bruiser, but rather a well-rounded back who also can contribute in the passing game as both a receiver from the backfield and in pass protection; he also is an experienced kickoff returner.

Hasty, meanwhile, has been in the league since 2020 — including one and a half years with the Patriots between the tail-end of 2023 and 2024. He has appeared in 61 total games and like Haskins has a versatile skillset that allows him to contribute on early downs, in passing situations, and in the kickoff return game. While a smaller player at 5-foot-8, 205 pounds, he nonetheless has shown his ability to be a multi-dimensional contributor.

Long story short, both Haskins and Hasty offer plug-and-play potential with the preseason about to kick off. With Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson unlikely to play meaningful snaps, especially on Thursday, they offer more depth at the position. Speaking of which…

Signing Haskins and Hasty, waiving Montgomery with the expectation that he will be placed on injured reserve, creates the following outlook for New England's running back group:

Running back (8): Rhamondre Stevenson (38), TreVeyon Henderson (32), Reggie Gilliam (44 | FB), Terrell Jennings (26), Lan Larison (34), Jam Miller (30), Hassan Haskins (—), JaMycal Hasty (—)

As things currently stand, the aforementioned Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson are roster locks; the same is true for Reggie Gilliam at fullback. The other spots on the roster, which could be as little as one, remain up for competition. Based on the last few training camp practices, however, Terrell Jennings appears to be the clear frontrunner.

Haskins and Hasty will get their opportunities, but any of them ending up on the 53-man team would either be a testament to their adaptation skills or the depth behind Stevenson and Henderson.

Besides their versatility and experience, Haskins and Hasty have something else in common. Both have spent time under Mike Vrabel before.

Haskins originally entered the NFL with the Titans in 2022, and spent his first two seasons in Tennessee. He played 15 games during that span, touching the ball 36 times for 150 yards on offense and returning 19 kickoffs for an average of 21.8 yards.

Hasty, meanwhile, is one of the few players on New England's current roster to have played under Bill Belichick, Jerod Mayo and Vrabel. His experience with the latter, however, is relatively minimal: he spent last year's training camp and preseason in Foxborough before his late-August release. Up until that point, he touched the ball 24 times for 91 yards in two exhibition games. Still, diving into the Josh McDaniels playbook is not entirely new for the 29-year-old.

While removing Montgomery from the active roster did not have an impact the Patriots' salary cap — his fully-guaranteed signing bonus proration was already part of the calculations — the signings of Haskins and Hasty do. Both come via identical one-year, $1.215 million minimum deals, although the expectation is that they qualify for the veteran salary benefit.

This, in turn, will allow the team to reduce their actual cap impact to $1.075 million. That is enough to make the Top 51 list, but the signings still change the books only minimally: New England loses a combined $70,000 in cap space because Andy Borregales' $1.005 million base salary gets bumped from Top 51 status.

Wednesday's transactions involving Haskins and Montgomery were a net-zero move from a roster perspective. Adding Hasty later on, however, does change the calculations: him being signed puts the Patriots above the 90-man roster limit and will force a follow-up move before it can be made official. That move can either be a release, move to injured reserve or trade — time will tell.

Of course, our Patriots roster count has them at 92 at the moment. However, offensive tackle Lorenz Metz has an exemption due to his international status. As a result, New England can actually carry 91 players on the active team.

title: Liverpool believe Ibrahim Mbaye deal is ‘too expensive’
description: Liverpool consider a deal for Paris Saint-Germain forward Ibrahim Mbaye to be ‘too expensive’, according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano.Liverpool are pushing to sign Mbaye, with the club loo...
fullText:
Liverpool consider a deal for Paris Saint-Germain forward Ibrahim Mbaye to be 'too expensive', according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano.

Liverpool are pushing to sign Mbaye, with the club looking to sign a natural right winger to replace Mohamed Salah.

The Reds have already held talks with his representatives over a potential move, but could be priced out of a move for the Senegal international.

PSG reportedly want close to €200 million for Mbaye and Bradley Barcola combined, an amount the Reds consider too steep.

The 18-year-old is the UEFA Champions League holders' youngest-ever starter, but has found it difficult to nail a starting berth. He is expected to leave this summer to get more playing time.

Bayer Leverkusen, FC Porto and RB Leipzig have also been linked with Mbaye, but the youngster prefers to join Liverpool.

It remains to be seen whether PSG would reduce their valuation to allow the right-winger to join the Reds.

Liverpool appear to be prioritising a move for Barcola, which could hinder Mbaye's move to the Merseyside giants.

Liverpool plan to use the France international as their left winger, with Rio Ngumoha moving to the right flank.

Liverpool could struggle next season if they fail to sign a natural right winger. Federico Chiesa is their only senior option in the position, but the Italian has struggled with injuries since joining the club.

The Reds should try to reach a compromise with PSG for Mbaye or look elsewhere for a right-wing specialist.

title: Cowboys Headlines: Parker's defense impresses, Rams' scrimmage POV

title: Barcelona forward’s move to PSG set to be completed today or tomorrow
description: After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and W...
fullText:
After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.

The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and World Cup campaign.

Ferran's move is currently of when and not if; with the player soon expected to travel to the French capital.

According to Cadena SER, the agreement between Barcelona and PSG for Ferran's transfer could be finalised between today and tomorrow.

Ferran Torres to soon become a PSG player. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The forward already has an agreement in place with the French club and is ready to travel to Paris in the coming hours to undergo his medical.

Ferran did not train with Barcelona on Thursday, having also been excused the previous day.

Negotiations between the two clubs have entered their final phase, with PSG having long since agreed personal terms with the player.

All that remains is for the definitive transfer terms to be settled, with the operation set to be closed for a figure of around €55 million.

For Barcelona, recouping such a sum for a player with just one year left on his contract represents excellent business, even if losing a World Cup final hero is far from ideal.

Ferran's exit could pave the way for Rodri to join Barcelona. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Ferran's exit is closely tied to Barcelona's other major ongoing operation, the pursuit of Rodri.

The Catalans have already sent Manchester City a second proposal worth €60 million, made up of a fixed fee and variables, having seen an initial €50 million bid rejected.

However, reports suggest City have also turned down this latest offer.

Barcelona remain confident the deal will ultimately happen, with the club planning to make a third and definitive offer in the region of €70 million, comprising €60 million fixed plus €10 million in add-ons.

The funds generated by Ferran's departure will naturally aid Barcelona's efforts to get the Rodri deal over the line, both financially and in terms of squad registration.

With one exit nearing completion, the Catalans will hope it paves the way for a marquee arrival, as they look to reshape their squad before the window closes.

title: Transfer rumour roundup: Man Utd brace for Bruno Fernandes bids; Spurs weigh move for Villarreal hotshot Georges Mikautadze
description: Thursday's transfer rumours feature Eduardo Camavinga, Folarin Balogun, and Martin Zubimendi.Manchester United are braced for interest in Bruno Fernandes before the transfer deadline. Juventus, AC Mil...
fullText:
Thursday's transfer rumours feature Eduardo Camavinga, Folarin Balogun, and Martin Zubimendi.

Manchester United are braced for interest in Bruno Fernandes before the transfer deadline. Juventus, AC Milan and Galatasaray are all keen on the midfielder, according to the BBC, whose deal expires in 2027. United, however, have no intention to sell and are working on a contract extension for the club captain.

Manchester United are also set to face disappointment in their pursuit of Real Madrid midfielderEduardo Camavinga. The Red Devils have expressed interest in the Frenchman, whose ability to cover central midfield and left-back adds to his appeal. However, The Athletic are reporting that Camavinga's clear preference is to stay in Spain.

Arsenal are reportedly prepared to listen to offers for Martin Zubimendi, following the signing of Bruno Guimaraes. TEAMtalk tell us that Zubimendi has piqued the interest of Chelsea and Real Madrid, who will need to cough up €90m (£77m) to secure his signature. Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso worked with Zubimendi at Real Sociedad and is open to a reunion.

Folarin Balogun is expected to leave AS Monaco this summer after an impressive World Cup with co-hosts the United States. However, Tottenham Hotspur have not made an approach for the ex-Arsenal goal-getter, confirms Fabrizio Romano. Galatasaray and Saudi sides are currently leading the race.

The North Londoners, however are considering Villarreal forwardGeorges Mikautadze. The Georgian scored 13 league goals during his debut season with The Yellow Submarine, and his entourage have also been contacted by Barcelona, say Transfer Feed.

Former Spurs loaneeJoao Palhinha could be set to return to the Premier League. The midfielder has agreed personal terms to join Aston Villa from Bayern Munich, though a fee is still to be agreed between the clubs.

Villa are hoping to addPalhinha to their depleted midfield, while the club are also in talks with West Ham over a deal for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. The Hammers have set an asking price of £25m for the right-back.

title: NFL analyst Damien Woody joins list of ESPN on-air talent cuts
description: Former Pro Bowl offensive lineman Damien Woody, who won two Super Bowls with the New England Patriots, will not have his contract renewed at ESPN.
fullText:
Two-time Super Bowl champion Damien Woody is the latest high-profile on-air personality to be let go by ESPN.

Woody, whose contract was not renewed, joins the list of recent layoffs which includes Ryan Clark, Cam Newton and Karl Ravech.

Woody, 48, played 12 seasons in the NFL as an offensive lineman for the New England Patriots, Detroit Lions and New York Jets. He made the Pro Bowl in 2002 and won two Super Bowl rings with the Patriots.

"Still processing it all but I want to thank all of my colleagues at ESPN who made it a joy to talk ball for 15 yrs," Woody wrote in a post on X. "Being a guy who had a serious speech impediment to working on tv was truly one of my proudest accomplishments. Looking forward to what God has in store for me next!"

Woody was a regular on a number of ESPN shows over the years, including "Get Up," "Fantasy Football Now" and "First Take." He also frequently appeared as an NFL analyst on "SportsCenter."

According to The Athletic, ESPN executives informed Woody of the decision a few weeks ago. He will continue to appear on the air through the end of the month.

title: Hodgkinson into 800m final after dramatic Werro fall
description: Keely Hodgkinson reaches the women's 800m final at the European Championships - moments after rival Audrey Werro suffers a dramatic fall that put her place in doubt.
fullText:
Keely Hodgkinson's bid for European gold continued as she stormed into the final of the women's 800m - moments after rival Audrey Werro suffered a dramatic fall that put her place in Friday's showpiece in doubt.

Werro - who ran the fastest time for 43 years earlier this season - led from the start in the first semi-final, but crashed to the floor on the final bend.

The Swiss 22-year-old got back to her feet a moment later and finished the race in last place, grimacing and clutching her chest.

However, Werro will race against Hodgkinson in a highly anticipated final following a successful appeal - despite footage showing she clipped her own leg before falling.

There was less drama in the second semi-final, with Hodgkinson safely crossing the line first in one minute 57.38 seconds.

The Olympic champion led from the start and held off the fast-improving Femke Broeders-Bol - a two-time world 400m hurdles champion who chose to switch events this season - to advance.

Asked if she had seen Werro's fall before her race, Hodgkinson told BBC TV: "I heard an 'ooh' [from the crowd] which is never a good sign. I don't know what it looked like."

Speaking before Werro's appeal, Hodgkinson added: "Obviously it's a real shame and I hope she's OK.

"I hope she's in the final tomorrow [Friday], that'd be a really exciting race."

The women's 800m has become the must-watch event of the championships because of the expected three-way battle between Hodgkinson, Werro and Broeders-Bol.

"The excitement makes me excited. I can't wait to step out there. It brings out the best in me," Hodgkinson added.

"I love a good challenge. Hopefully it'll be a good race, a clean race, nobody falling over."

Hodgkinson will be joined in the final by fellow Briton Jemma Reekie, who capitalised on Werro's fall to win the first semi-final.

There will be 10 athletes in Friday's final instead of nine, with Lithuanian athlete Gabija Galvydyte - who was clipped by Werro as she fell - also advancing alongside the Swiss.

title: Thanks to Yankees teammate, Jasson Dominguez made a change that could unleash Martian
description: A week after being demoted by the Yankees to Triple-A, Jasson Dominguez met up with NJ.com before a game this week in Allentown, Pennsylvania.
fullText:
ALLENTOWN, Pa. — Jasson Dominguez used to think that he was one of the hardest workers on his teams, and why not?

He always showed up on time. He always gave an honest effort. He never took shortcuts. He never got big-headed when the Yankees gave him a $5.1 million signing bonus at age 16 or when he was being compared to all-time greats before he played his first game as a professional.

Whether Dominguez was in the minors or was with the Yankees, he always cared about improving in all parts of his game, especially his fielding.

An American League scout who has watched Dominguez since he was playing Low-A ball in Tampa agreed.

"He never dogged it," the scout told NJ.com recently. "He worked hard. But he never was the hardest worker on his club. There was always someone next to him on the field giving more effort. It was noticeable that Dominguez wasn't going above and beyond to get better when others around him with half his talent were."

When that assessment was shared with Dominguez on Tuesday night before he played left field for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, he responded with a smile and a nod.

"Oh, definitely," Dominguez said. "For sure. I've always worked hard, but definitely now I'm working more than what I used to do. That's from being in the big leagues and having great teammates."

Dominguez's work habits began changing late last season. When the Yankees upgraded their bench by trading for Amed Rosario, the hard-working journeyman infielder took Dominguez, a fellow Dominican, under his wing.

"Rosario is the guy that pushed me," Dominguez said. "He's a guy that literally came early every day to do his work and I started doing that with him."

When Rosario re-signed with the Yankees last winter, he pushed Dominguez during their spring training workouts on and off the field. Dominguez maintained a hard-working mentality when he started this season in the minors through his time with the Yankees, which also featured a stint on the injured list for a shoulder injury.

Rosario and Dominguez were separated again on Aug. 3, when the Yankees acquired outfielder Heliot Ramos at the trade deadline and rookie Spencer Jones was picked over Dominguez to remain in the majors.

Back with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, Dominguez no longer needs anyone to motivate him.

"I felt pretty good with Rosario around and now I keep doing it because I understand that I've got things that I need to improve," Dominguez said. "I understand what needs to be done now. It's working harder than I ever worked, trying to get better and hopefully get back up to the big leagues."

Dominguez has been improving. In his first few years as a professional, Dominguez was so much better as a left-handed hitter that some scouts suggested that he give up batting right-handed. This year, he's been better as a right-handed hitter.

His outfield play is still below average, but his minus-1 Outs Above Average ranking in Baseball Savant's metrics is much better than last season's worst-in-the-league minus-9.

"I see a player who's constantly getting better, and that's the most important thing," RailRiders manager Shelley Duncan said. "Jasson has been in the spotlight a lot, and when you make mistakes with fundamentals or make mental errors in New York, it gets highlighted more than anywhere else in all of baseball.

"If you like take a guy like Jasson and that stuff happened in other places, it might slide under the radar and not even get noticed and you just chalk it up as a young guy learning. I say that because all of the mistakes that Jasson's made over his career, he learned from them and I've seen him grow as a player."

Dominguez will tell you that he's not close to his prime. He wants to live up to his Martian nickname and comparisons from his teenage years to Yankees legend Mickey Mantle and present-day superstar Mike Trout. That's a far-fetched dream, but he still has time to develop into an All-Star.

"I hope one day I can meet those reputations for sure, but at the end of the day, Mike Trout is Mike Trout and Mickey Mantle is Mickey Mantle," Dominguez said. "They've already done it. I'm trying to grow myself to be able to do it, too."

His opening act as a big leaguer featured a first-inning homer in his first game in Houston off future Hall of Famer Justin Verlander. He was 20 on Sept. 1, 2023. A few days later, he was headed for Tommy John surgery.

Almost three years later, he's been a mixed bag of highs, lows and more injuries. He's a career .243 hitter with 22 homers, 72 RBI, 36 steals and a .703 OPS in 741 plate appearances over 202 games.

In 2025, Dominguez batted .257 with 10 homers and 47 RBI in 123 games, but his fielding woes led to virtually no playing time in the final two months before he was sent back to Triple-A to open 2026.

He's crushed it in Triple-A this year, hitting .313 with six homers and 21 RBI in 33 games, but his numbers in 53 games with the Yankees were disappointing — .230 with six homers and 14 RBI in 53 games, most of them filling in right field for injured three-time MVP Aaron Judge.

"Jasson has what it takes to be really good," Scranton bench coach Gil Velazquez said. "He's disciplined. He's a good baseball player, period. He's still young and it takes a good amount of reps to be able to not get surprised with situations and not make dumb mistakes. Everybody goes through that."

Dominguez is still going through it. In his last full series, he misplayed a couple of balls in the right field corner at Wrigley Field. These were unforced mistakes in his mind, and they upset him.

"I want to improve the mental side," he said. "I have to make better decisions. That's one thing that I need to get better at."

That's part of the reason Dominguez is back in the minors.

After being optioned, he spent the allotted 72 hours he had to report to Triple-A at his New Jersey home with his family.

"I used those three days to reset my mind so I could go to Scranton with the best attitude," he said. "Obviously, I want to be in the big leagues, but it is what it is now. If I came down here with a bad attitude and pouted or whatever, that's not gonna help me get back up."

Dominguez trusts the Yankees are doing what's best for his career. He's focused.

"I want to improve my whole game," he said.

Slowly but surely, it's growing.

"He cut a ball down in the left-field corner and threw a runner out at second the other day," Duncan bragged. "His decision making and throwing is a lot better in the outfield this year. His focus pitch to pitch has gotten better every time I've seen him.

"It's fun watching Jasson hit because he's a carefree-loose type of hitter that can hit any type of pitcher. Those are fun hitters to have. He's got the talent and skillset to be a really good big leaguer for a long time."

title: Keely Hodgkinson’s main rival advanced to 800m final after shock fall
description: Audrey Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year, fell and finished last – but was advanced to the 10-athlete final following an appeal
fullText:
Keely Hodgkinson's main rival, Audrey Werro, was advanced to the 800m final at the European Athletics Championships after a shock result in her semi-final as she fell hard and finished last.

Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year, led the first semi-final from the start and responded to accelerations from Britain's Jemma Reekie and French record holder Anais Bourgoin.

But the 22-year-old appeared to be clipped from behind on the final bend and hit the deck hard, with Lithuania's Gabija Galvydyte also falling as the other runners attempted to evade the fallen Swiss.

Both athletes eventually got to their feet and finished the race, with Werro crossing the line last looking heavily winded and clutching her ribs. Referees advanced both her and Galvydyte to the final after appeals, meaning 10 athletes will race for the title on Friday.

Hodgkinson eased to victory in her semi-final, winning in 1:57.38 from Femke Broeders-Bol, who looked comfortable on her shoulder in an unfamiliar event for the Dutchwoman, having stepped up from her usual 400m hurdles this year. The result leaves the pair and Werro on course for a blockbuster clash in Friday's final.

Werro told the BBC afterwards: "I was feeling really great until the last metre, unfortunately, I don't know, something happened and I was on the ground. I hope I will be qualified for the final."

She confirmed that she kept running in order to be able to appeal for a place in the final, if video replays suggested she was hindered by another athlete: "This is the reason why I finished the race and it's always important to go until the end, now we will see what happened."

Reekie came through to win the semi-final in 1:58.61, with Bourgoin and Switzerland's Veronica Vancardo completing the trio of automatic qualifiers.

Werro ran the fastest time in four decades earlier this season, with her new personal best of 1:53.80 the third-fastest of all time, making her the favourite to take gold in Birmingham's Alexander Stadium despite the presence of Olympic champion Hodgkinson and Broeders-Bol.

In the second semi-final Hodgkinson hit the front early with Broeders-Bol latching onto her shoulder, with the pair pulling away in the home straight. Italy's Eloisa Coiro, who set a new national record in the first round, was the last of the automatic qualifiers. Switzerland's Valentina Rosamilia and France's Clara Liberman complete the line-up for the final.

Hodgkinson was asked by BBC Sport whether she had seen Werro's fall. She said: "I heard a 'oohhh' [from the crowd] which is never a good sign; I don't know what it looked like," she said. "You can't worry about what other people are doing [in your race]. It's a real shame, I hope she's okay and that she's in the final tomorrow.

"The depth was really good, another 1:57, overall happy, can't complain. The excitement [for the women's 800m] makes me excited, I love a good challenge, it brings out the best in me.

"I hope for a clean race with no falling over. And no wind please, I'm going to talk to an Esty witch to make sure there's no wind," she smiled.

Broeders-Bol meanwhile said seeing Werro fall had made her feel "extra cautious" in her semi. She said her plan had been to lead "from the front, either with Keely or in front of Keely, I think it worked out perfectly.

"I saw it [the fall], I didn't watch a replay because it often looks terrible. I hope she's okay. It made me extra cautious."

title: Will West Ham bounce straight back up?
description: BBC Sport analyses the season ahead for West Ham, who will be playing in the Championship for the first time in 14 years.
fullText:
When Declan Rice hoisted the Europa Conference League trophy aloft in 2023, few would have envisaged that West Ham United would be preparing for life in the Championship just three years later.

A first major trophy for 43 years followed a Europa League semi-final the season before and would be backed up by another European quarter-final in 2024.

The Hammers also finished sixth and seventh in the Premier League in 2021 and 2022.

It was an era for the east London club in which relative success had become the norm.

But things can change quickly in football and for the first time in 14 years, West Ham will be playing outside the top flight.

The Irons are the favourites for an instant return to the Premier League, which they achieved in 2011-12, though the English Football League (EFL) can be an unforgiving environment, even for a club boasting the biggest stadium in Championship history.

And with an ownership tug of war playing out behind the scenes, which way will it go for West Ham in the 2026-27 campaign? BBC Sport takes a look.

This is a path well trodden by other big clubs in English football in recent history.

Newcastle United have dealt with adversity with relative ease on the two occasions they have been relegated to the Championship, in 2010 and 2017, and bounced straight back.

Aston Villa dragged themselves back following relegation in 2016, but it took three years, including a 13th-placed finish in their first season in the second tier followed by a play-off final defeat before eventual promotion.

But Leicester City, Blackburn Rovers and Leeds United fans can all attest to just how quickly the situation can spiral once a team is sucked into the EFL grind.

Leicester were Premier League champions 10 years ago. This season they will be playing in League One, just two years after relegation from the top flight.

Blackburn lifted the title in 1995 and enjoyed several European campaigns along the way.

But Rovers were relegated to the Championship in 2012 - and to League One in 2017. They are yet to get out of the EFL.

Similarly in 2005, Leeds were relegated just four years on from a Champions League semi-final and one year after a UEFA Cup campaign.

It would take 16 years and a journey down to the third tier before Leeds played in the Premier League again.

It was Jarrod Bowen who netted the dramatic last-minute winner for West Ham against Fiorentina on that memorable night of European glory in June 2023 to etch his name into the club's history books.

And Bowen committing his future to the club is perhaps better than any summer signing West Ham could have made.

Bowen has been the club's top goalscorer in four of the past five seasons, netting 76 times in 227 games in all competitions.

He has also provided 53 assists and signalled his intent for the current campaign in Saturday's 3-1 victory over Portsmouth in the EFL Cup, scoring one and setting up another.

An England international, a player of his pedigree could prove invaluable.

"It was a no-brainer for me to be here and the vision is clear," said Bowen after confirming he would stay at the London Stadium. "It's the Premier League."

But the 29-year-old is fully aware of the challenge the Championship provides.

"It's 46 tough games, midweek, Saturday, Tuesday, Friday," Bowen said.

"There's going to be disappointment at times, there's going to be a lot of pressure on us to go and win the league straight away.

"That's our aim, but I'm telling you now, it's not going to be as easy as that."

Manager Nuno Espirito Santo agrees.

"Normally when a team drops to the Championship, you have to be the favourite, mainly because our objective is to go back to the Premier League," the 52-year-old told BBC Radio London.

"We realise how hard it's going to be. We're going to have to be resilient, to keep going.

"Tight schedule, very tough competition, a lot of good teams with the same aspirations as ourselves.

"But we are ready for the challenge."

Retention of key personnel is arguably the most important factor for the Hammers in 2026-27.

Nuno's choice to remain is a luxury not every relegated side always has - Burnley start the season with a new boss, Nicky Hayen, and likewise Wolves with Cesar Peixoto.

Nuno has been there and done it before at this level with Wolves, winning the Championship to gain promotion in 2017-18.

"I look at West Ham as being the team that has kept hold of an incredible manager," ex-Nottingham Forest and Ipswich Town defender Luke Chambers told the BBC's 72+ podcast.

"I think it's a massive coup. It's almost like having an £80m signing coming in. He is top, top level."

There is a proverbial elephant in the room at West Ham though, with an ongoing ownership saga.

Relegation made high-profile player departures inevitable.

Midfielder Mateus Fernandes signed for Tottenham for £85m, winger Crysencio Summerville joined Saudi club Al-Hilal in a deal worth £60m and Freddie Potts, who came through the West Ham academy, has gone to Belgian champions Club Brugge.

Those exits, in theory, should allow West Ham to reinvest that money.

But with a £104.2m loss in their most recent accounts, new Squad Cost Rules (SCR) to comply with and Amanda Staveley's co-ownership struggle, it is not as simple as splashing out every penny of that £150m to overhaul the squad.

The situation is complex and likely to drag on for several months into the new season.

A consortium led by Staveley - the former Newcastle United co-owner - has agreed to buy the Gold family's 25% stake in the club.

But current co-chair Daniel Kretinsky has publicly opposed Staveley's deal, and appears to be working hard to keep her from getting a foot in the door.

Nuno insists funding for transfers is not a problem.

"It's not about the money. We don't have too much time, but what we can't afford is mistakes," Nuno said.

"We have to make it right. To avoid mistakes is crucial this year. The player that comes in the door has to have the same purpose and be identified with the mission we have ahead."

Glyn: Boardroom issues, inevitably, filter down to the pitch. With this wrangling going on, how is it possible to plan? Not many incomings, so far, and the uncertainty surrounding ownership will not aid that process.

Dave: The way this board and its advisors are working, I can see us doing a Luton, which is sadly nothing more than they deserve. I have supported this club for 58 years and I can not remember a worse time.

Andy: Recruitment, as ever, will be the problem, and I predict after a standard very slow start, we'll finish 5th, missing out in the play-off final.

Brendan: If West Ham can't begin to iron out their very obvious off-field problems, they won't have a chance in the Championship.

How will relegated trio fare in the Championship?

Fighting relegation & eyeing promotion? Championship set for six-team play-offs

Despite concerns from some supporters, those working in the game still expect West Ham to challenge at the top.

"I don't think they will be a Leicester," said Bromley manager Andy Woodman.

"They're a little bit more stable than Leicester were. If they can get a few early results and get that fan base on board, it could be massive. I think West Ham will be a force to beat this year."

Former Nottingham Forest striker Lyle Taylor also believes West Ham's home support - with 50,000 season tickets sold - could be crucial.

"If the fans decide 'we're behind the team, we're behind the manager, we're going to push them over the line,' then I can see West Ham winning the Championship at a canter," he said.

West Ham's squad will take on a fresh appearance when they visit Burnley in their first Championship game of the season on Sunday.

Centre-back Axel Disasi has returned to Chelsea and Callum Wilson has joined Brentford, while Fernandes, Summerville and Potts are long gone.

Winger Manor Solomon, who scored 10 goals in 39 Championship games to help Leeds United win promotion in 2024-25, has arrived from Tottenham for £5m.

Ex-Brighton defender Joel Veltman, 34, has also joined, while Mexico international Edson Alvarez has returned from a loan spell with Fenerbahce, as have James Ward-Prowse from Burnley and George Earthy from Bristol City.

There is still time for further additions and West Ham already have the core of a competitive team.

Keeping hold of key starters attracting interest, including defender Konstantinos Mavropanos, will also be essential to an immediate return to the top flight.

"We are going to face the pressure, that's our job," goalkeeper Mads Hermansen told BBC Radio London. "We are West Ham, we are the biggest club in the league and we want to show that we are going straight back up."

Strong words from the Dane, even if promotion is unlikely to be a formality. Nothing ever is in the Championship.

title: Morrison targeting improvement not play-off talk
description: West Bromwich Albion will target improvement after last term's relegation battle says boss James Morrison.
fullText:
West Bromwich Albion head coach James Morrison refused to be drawn on the club's chances of being in the mix for the newly-expanded play-offs, instead insisting this season was all about doing better than last.

Given the club's close shave with relegation last term, and the current limits of their spending power, Morrison does not want to start adding to the levels of expectation on his players before a ball is kicked in the Championship.

"I don't want to get too carried away, I don't want to put any more pressure on us but I think as a group we know where we want to get to," he told BBC Radio WM.

"We know what we have to do to get there and we have to remain good on the training pitch, competitive in the games, understanding what we've got to do.

"It's just hard work. You can have all the best tactics in the world but if the hard work's not there, we may as well stay at home."

From this season, two more play-off spots are available allowing teams finishing seventh and eighth to now have a shot a reaching the Premier League.

Albion, who last reached the play-offs in 2024, ended last term four points above the relegation zone in 21st after a tough campaign on and off the field.

With that in mind, Morrison, who said he feels "ready" for the new season said his main priority is to see an uptick on 2025-26 even though he thought more play-off contenders was a good idea.

"I'll welcome it. It means you have to give it an opportunity to keep going to the end of the season," he said.

"It gives more teams opportunities. It doesn't create that divide of same teams always being in around it. It gives the lesser teams a chance and I think a little change in football is always exciting and not be predictable.

"I'm not going to get into that [whether Albion's chances are improved] but I think for me at the start it's just about improving."

Albion start their Championship campaign at Norwich City on Saturday (15:00 BST).

title: Report: Chelsea attacker set to head to Premier League new boys
description: Mykhailo Mudryk Loan Latest as Coventry City Monitor Chelsea Winger SituationChelsea are open to loan offers for Mykhailo Mudryk following his return to competitive action, according to Football Londo...
fullText:
Chelsea are open to loan offers for Mykhailo Mudryk following his return to competitive action, according to Football London, with Coventry City among the clubs watching developments closely ahead of the transfer deadline.

The 25-year-old has re-entered the picture after disciplinary proceedings were resolved, ending a long period on the sidelines. Mudryk had not featured competitively since November 2024, but he did make brief appearances in Chelsea's final three pre-season matches, a sign that he is back in circulation as the club weighs up the next step.

There is interest from multiple Premier League sides and Coventry's presence in that group stands out. Frank Lampard knows the player from their time together at Stamford Bridge, and that prior relationship could become relevant if Chelsea do decide that a temporary move is the best route for all parties. From Chelsea's side, there is a clear need to balance the player's pathway with a crowded attacking unit.

Xabi Alonso has publicly left the matter open, saying, "No decision made. We need to assess, he is a special player but it is a special case so we need to be sensitive." That line captures the tone around this situation. Chelsea are not rushing, but they are assessing a market in which a loan looks realistic.

Strasbourg also remain a viable solution. Chelsea can still send one more player on loan to their sister club under current FIFA rules, with Genesis Antwi and Filip Jorgensen already moving there. Dastan Satpayev is another name in that conversation, which means there are internal decisions to make over how that final slot is used.

From Coventry's perspective, the attraction is obvious. Mudryk brings top-level experience, speed and unpredictability, and although consistency has often been the question, the talent has never been in doubt. A player of his profile would add a different dimension to Lampard's forward line if a deal became achievable.

Any move would also depend on Chelsea's view of his immediate role. Morgan Rogers has emerged as the leading left-sided option, while Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda have both strengthened their cases during pre-season. Pedro Neto can operate on either flank and remains available for the right fee, which leaves competition for places intense.

With three weeks remaining in the window, this feels like a situation moving towards clarity rather than one already decided. Chelsea have options, Coventry have interest and Mudryk has a chance to reset his career with regular football. For now, the key detail is straightforward, a loan is on the table, and Coventry City are firmly in the frame.

As a Coventry fan, this is exactly the sort of report that gets you thinking about what might be possible under Frank Lampard. Mudryk has had a difficult spell, but there is a serious player in there and sometimes a fresh environment is what unlocks everything. If Coventry really are in the mix, then it speaks volumes about the ambition around the club right now.

The biggest reason for encouragement is Lampard himself. He knows the player, knows the personality and will have a clear idea of whether Mudryk could thrive in his system. That matters. Coventry would not be taking a blind gamble here, they would be moving for someone the manager understands.

There is also a footballing upside that is easy to see. Coventry supporters want players who can turn a match in seconds, carry the ball, commit defenders and inject real pace into the attack. Mudryk does all of that. If he arrived with a point to prove, the energy around the CBS Arena would be huge.

Of course, there would be risks. Match sharpness, confidence and expectation would all need careful handling. But on loan, with Chelsea still carrying the long-term picture, this could be the kind of opportunity worth chasing. For Coventry, it would feel bold, exciting and full of upside.

title: Infantino’s FIFA fate must go to an election, says Africa football chief
description: CAF have given under-fire Gianni Infantino their backing, and now say the FIFA president must stand in March’s election.
fullText:
Africa football confederation chief Patrice Motsepe says Gianni Infantino's future should only be decided by elections, after Ireland became the latest federation to withdraw its support for the embattled FIFA president.

Infantino is fighting to save his job after a barrage of criticism for his aborted plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The governing bodies of European football (UEFA), North and Central America (CONCACAF) and Asia (AFC) stepped up the pressure on Infantino in a joint letter this week, declaring "trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority."

It is believed they want Infantino to resign before he has the chance to seek re-election in March next year.

But Motsepe, a FIFA vice president and Confederation of Africa Football (CAF) president, is adamant that Infantino's fate should be decided through the ballot box.

"If anybody has got any problem against anybody, whether it's Gianni, whether it is anybody else, follow the process, follow the FIFA process, simple as that," Motsepe told Sky News on Thursday.

"If you want to take him out, go for elections; let the 211 member associations decide. Do that and the vote will express whether they've got confidence in him or not.

"You've got to be very careful. There are elections taking place next year. Shouldn't we allow that process to continue?"

Motsepe was in Salzburg at the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday to hold talks with UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, whose organisation are threatening to boycott the World Cup and Club World Cup in protest at Infantino's scheme.

"I've heard so many stories about various issues and am careful to pass judgement on anything," Motsepe said.

"Everybody has a right to be heard. Let's have a hearing, and a proper forum."

CAF had already backed Infantino, and Motsepe claimed there was no breach of rules over the World Cup sell-off talks because the proposals would be submitted to FIFA members for final approval.

"There's a lot that's problematic and negative that they have to fix," Motsepe said.

"But he has apologised and said maybe there's a different way these things should have been done, but we also take advice."

However, there has been no end to the tidal wave of criticism engulfing Infantino.

On Thursday, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) became the latest FIFA member to withdraw its support for Infantino.

"Following an FAI Board Meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," the organisation said.

"It has since written to FIFA to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that FIFA provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation."

The English FA and Welsh FA had already withdrawn their backing for the 56-year-old Swiss.

Six Arab federations, including Qatar, Morocco and Egypt, offered their backing to Infantino on Thursday morning.

title: Broncos host former Rams 2nd-round safety for tryout
description: Taylor Rapp is currently a free agent but the Denver Broncos are giving the former Los Angeles Rams safety a look.
fullText:
Former Los Angeles Rams safety Taylor Rapp remains a free agent after being cut by the Buffalo Bills this offseason, but another AFC powerhouse is giving him a look. According to reports, the Denver Broncos hosted Rapp for a tryout on Wednesday.

Rapp, 28, played just six games for the Bills last season before being placed on injured reserve with a knee injury. It was the second year of a three-year contract he signed with the Bills in 2024, worth a total of $10.62 million. The Bills originally signed him to a one-year deal in 2023 after the Rams let him walk in free agency.

During his four years with the Rams, Rapp played 57 games and made 48 starts, picking off nine passes with 330 total tackles. He was part of the 2021 Super Bowl team, starting that game and making seven tackles in the win over the Bengals.

If the Broncos end up signing Rapp, he'll get a chance to face his former team in Week 3 when the Rams play Denver on the road.

title: 'Same players making the same mistakes' - Howey
description: Newcastle players were making the "same mistakes" in their 3-1 loss to Everton in pre-season on Wednesday, says former Magpies defender Steve Howey.  The Premier League returns next week and Howey believes Matthias Jaissle's side need the time to work on the same issues from last season.  "I was just a little bit disappointed at half-time because it's familiar players - the players that will be making the starting line-up against Liverpool - that are making the same mistakes again," Howey told BBC Radio Newcastle after the match.
fullText:
Newcastle players were making the "same mistakes" in their 3-1 loss to Everton in pre-season on Wednesday, says former Magpies defender Steve Howey.

The Premier League returns next week and Howey believes Matthias Jaissle's side need the time to work on the same issues from last season.

"I was just a little bit disappointed at half-time because it's familiar players - the players that will be making the starting line-up against Liverpool - that are making the same mistakes again," Howey told BBC Radio Newcastle after the match.

"And I'm talking missing chances, even though they might be half-chances and some of them were but some of them were more than half-chances.

"When you've got the ball getting drilled into you, make it stick, but it's bouncing off players, and I'm just thinking we used to see that last season. And I know there's been the World Cup, and you have still got time to work on these things - it's not going to improve straight away, it's going to take time. But it was just annoying because it is the same players making the same mistakes again.

"They'll have a little bit of a breather as such, they'll stretch off and do whatever they have to do, but then go again at the weekend with the two games before getting really ready for the start of the season. Only they'll know individually and collectively if they're ready, but whether they're ready or not, it's coming."

title: SN 140: The top college football teams of each decade dating back to the 1800s
description: See how the bluebloods became the bluebooods.
fullText:
SN 140: The top college football teams of each decade dating back to the 1800s originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

College football has been evolving in hyperspeed the last five years and shows no signs of slowing down. And yet, the more things change ...

As part of Sporting News' year-long celebration of 140 years of publishing, we took a look back at a sport that loves its history and traditions perhaps more than any other in the U.S. Last week, SN named seven All-Decade All-America teams, starting in the 1960s. This week, we are going all the way back, to when we published our first newspaper, when touchdowns were four points and field goals were worth five. We are naming our top program of each decade -- with some being obvious and some being absolutely not obvious.

But it is interesting to note, teams that were at the top of the sport in the '40s, '50s, '60s, '70s and '80s will be contending for College Football Playoff spots in 2026. If you want to learn how the modern-day bluebloods of the sport became blueboods, read about their dominance from decades ago.

We hope you enjoy your trip back in time as we look ahead to 140 more years of publishing (and college football!).

SN 140 ALL-AMERICA TEAMS BY DECADE:2020s|2010s | 2000s | 1990s | 1980s | 1970s | 1960s

SN 140: Greatest college football teams of all time

National titles: 1874, 1876, 1877, 1880, 1881, 1882, 1883, 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1891, 1892, 1894

Why they are here: By the time The Sporting News published its first newspaper in 1886, Yale had put together 10 unbeaten seasons and were retroactively awarded eight national championships by the National Championship Foundation. The following 15 seasons brought more glory, as Walter Camp became the team's first official coach in 1888 and proceeded to go 68-2 in his first five seasons. (Princeton and Harvard bested the Yaleies). Captains served as coach before then, and Camp was the captain for three of his playing seasons. He was also instrumental in several rule changes that slowly made the violent, brutal nature of the first iterations of the game slightly less violent and brutal.

Honorable mention: Princeton and Harvard gave Yale the most competition, and Penn emerged late in the 1890s, but had stopped playing Yale at that point. The only non-Ivy League school to claim a national championship in the 1800s was 1896 Lafayette, which went 11-0-1 with the tie coming against Princeton.

National titles: 1901, 1902, 1903, 1904

Why they are here: Fielding Yost took the reins of the Michigan program in 1901 and proceeded to steamroll everything in its path in his first five years. Michigan went 11-0 in his first year and beat Stanford 49-0 in the Rose Bowl, finishing the season with 550 points scored and 0 allowed. In '02, they allowed six points during another perfect season. A 6-6 tie against Minnesota was the only blemish in 1903 and 1904 produced another perfect season that included a 130-0 win over West Virginia. The Wolverines were 55-1-1 in Yost's first five seasons. They outscored Ohio State 285-18 for the decade, finishing 9-0-1 against their rivals.

Honorable mention: Yale notched 100 wins, with most coming against major competition as college football was more established in the Northeast. The Bulldogs were awarded the 1900, 1907 and 1909 national titles, plus had undefeated seasons in 1902, 1905 and 1906. Princeton, Penn and Harvard were also Northeast powers, while Michigan's competition in the Midwest came from Chicago under Amos Alonzo Stagg and Minnesota.

Why they are here: John Heisman (yes, the Trophy guy) had quite a run in Atlanta, going 24-0-2 from 1915-17 against what was considered a difficult schedule at the time. Included in that stretch was the Yellow Jackets' infamous 222-0 win over Cumberland. The 1917 national championship team gave up just 17 points in nine games and Tech had a winning record all 10 years of the decade.

Honorable mention: Minnesota remained a Western Conference power with a 52-13-4 record. Pitt was retroactively awarded three national titles in 1910, 1916 and 1918 (with a war-shortened 4-1 record), the latter two under coach Pop Warner. Pitt matched Georgia Tech by going undefeated from 1915-17. Vanderbilt and Auburn were consistently elite, and Harvard owned New England football at the time with a gaudy 65-7-5 record.

Why they are here: Knute Rockne took over in 1918, went undefeated in 1919 and rolled through the '20s suffering either no losses or one loss in eight of the 10 seasons. Legend has it he was an early adopter of the forward pass, and his Irish traveled coast-to-coast and created a national following. By 1928, ND went east to play Penn State, south to play Georgia Tech and west to play USC. That type of travel was unique to the Irish at the time.

Honorable mention: Cal picked up two national titles and had five undefeated seasons while winning at an .805 percentage for the decade. Vanderbilt (68-17-7) and Alabama (74-21-6) were early powers in the new Southern Conference. Cornell went 24-0 from 1921-23 under Gilmour Dobie, though the 1923 national title went to Champions of the West(ern Conference) – Michigan.

National titles: 1934, 1935, 1936

Minnesota won the first AP national championship in 1936 after a pair of undefeated seasons in 1934 and 1935 that were retroactively awarded national titles by the Helms Athletic Foundation and the NCF. Coach Bernie Bierman had a record of 93-35-6 from 1932-50.

Honorable mention: Notre Dame was 66-20-5 (.753) with just nine winning seasons in a decade where the program had to overcome the loss of coach Knute Rockne in a plane crash after his undefeated 1930 season. ND wasn't able to quite match the gold standard Rockne established but remained elite. USC won 72 games and was 30-2-1 with two Rose Bowl wins from 1931-33. Alabama was 79-11 but somehow did not win a national championship.

National titles: 1943, 1946, 1947, 1949

Why they are here: When World War II ended, Notre Dame fielded a juggernaut that did not lose a game for four years. Frank Leahy's squad went 36-0-2 in the first four seasons after the war, which added to a 1943 national title led by Heisman winner Angelo Bertelli. The Irish claimed two other Heismans in the decade as well and was the sport's dominant program.

Honorable mention: Army went a perfect 16-0 with back-to-back national titles in 1944-45 and went 9-0-1 in 1946 with a famous 0-0 tie against Notre Dame. Army won 67 games, two Heismans and was ranked in seven of the 10 seasons. Minnesota started the decade with a pair of undefeated, national championship seasons led by 1941 Heisman winner Bruce Smith.

National titles: 1950, 1955, 1956

Why they are here: The team that put together a mid-decade 47-game winning streak was a pretty clear winner. That streak remains unmatched at the FBS level. The Sooners won three consensus national titles, which was not an easy thing to do with four outlets declaring national champions (1954, 1957 and 1958 were all split). OU was ranked all 10 years and only twice lost more than one game. Bud Wilkinson's squad ruled the decade.

Honorable mention: Ohio State won one AP national title in 1954 and a UPI national title in 1957 after winning Rose Bowls under Woody Hayes. Bobby Dodd was 79-26-6 at Georgia Tech playing in the SEC, including 6-0 in bowl games. Ole Miss won 80 games and finished No. 2 in 1959, and Notre Dame ended OU's winning streak and had three Top 5 finishes.

National titles: 1961, 1964, 1965 (split)

Overall record: 90-16-4 (55-12-2 SEC)

Why they are here: Bear Bryant quickly restored power in Tuscaloosa after Jennings Whitworth went 4-24-2 from 1955-57. By the time the '60s rolled around, the Tide was ready to roll through the decade. The 1965 'split' title was only split because UPI voted before bowl games and gave Michigan State the title before the Spartans lost the Rose Bowl. In 1966, 11-0 Alabama finished behind Notre Dame and Michigan State, who went undefeated but tied each other. Bama finished in the top 5 five times in the '60s.

Honorable mention: Texas won consensus titles in 1963 and 1969 and piled up 86 wins. One ding to the resume was four seasons where the Longhorns finished unranked. USC matches Texas with two national titles and two unranked seasons, and adds Heismans from O.J. Simpson and Mike Garrett. Woody Hayes had Ohio State rolling as well with one national title and four top five finishes, but there were five seasons the Buckeyes finished unranked.

National titles: 1974 (split), 1975

Why they are here: Oklahoma owned the best winning percentage among major programs, it won two AP national championships, and would have had two UPI national championships if Barry Switzer's undefeated 1974 team wasn't on probation (UPI did not vote for teams on probation). The Sooners had an average final ranking of 4.7 in the AP poll and were ranked all 10 seasons, plus produced Heisman Trophy winner Billy Sims. OU went 7-3 vs. Nebraska, which averaged 9.8 wins per year.

Honorable mention: USC was right there, with 1 AP and 3 UPI national titles (including the above-mentioned '74). It was ranked all 10 years, won 93 games and owned a very good ND program. Alabama won 90 percent of its SEC games and 103 games overall, and was only hurt by a 6-5-1 record in 1970. Nebraska won two AP national titles and finished ranked all 10 years, and Notre Dame averaged 9.2 wins per season for the decade and also won two AP national titles. This decade was the toughest debate.

National titles: 1983, 1987, 1989

Why they are here: Miami's three national titles came under three different head coaches, with Howard Schnellenberger shocking Nebraska in 1983, Jimmy Johnson steamrolling to an undefeated season in 1987 and Dennis Erickson capping the decade with a third championship. The Hurricanes also had two No. 2 finishes in the AP poll and won their final 32 games at the Orange Bowl (bowl games included) in the 1980s.

Honorable mention: Nebraska won 103 games and finished in the AP Top 11 every year. A 4-6 record in bowl games and no national championships are the only negatives on the resume. The 1983 team lost 31-30 to Miami in the Orange Bowl after winning their first 12 games by an average of 36 points. Oklahoma had four Top 6 seasons, won four Big 8 titles over Nebraska, won 91 games and the '85 national championship. Penn State won 89 games and two national titles, but had four unranked seasons.

Overall record: 109-13 (62-2 ACC)

Why they are here: The most amazing FSU stat for the '90s? The Seminoles finished in the AP Top 4 all 10 seasons. Florida State went an incredible 109-13 and captured national titles in 1993 and 1999. It was a tight battle with Nebraska for Program of the Decade, but the Noles finished ahead of the Huskers in the AP poll seven times. FSU also won both head-to-head matchups, beating them in the Fiesta Bowl after the 1992 season and the Orange Bowl in the 1993 season that gave Bobby Bowden his first national title. The 1999 squad was the first wire-to-wire No. 1 team of the AP era.

Honorable mention: In Tom Osborne's final five seasons from 1993-97, Nebraska lost just three games. The Huskers also closed the decade with a 12-1 season in 1999. The Huskers finished in the top 6 six times and the 1995 team is considered one of the sport's best of all time. FSU's two head-to-head wins give it the slightest of edges over Nebraska here.

National titles: 2004, 2005 (split)

Overall record: 102-26 (64-20 Pac-10)

Why they are here: This one was tight. USC opened the decade with a couple of duds, but Pete Carroll got things rolling to the point that his 2005 team was being discussed as the best of all time … before it lost in the final seconds to Texas and Vince Young in one of the great games of all time. Carson Palmer, Reggie Bush and Matt Leinart all won Heismans, and USC was 37-2 from 2003-05. The final eight years of the decade, USC went 13-0 vs. the Big Ten/SEC and 8-0 against Notre Dame.

Honorable mention: Florida and LSU both had claims as both won more than one national title. The Gators had two championships in three years, with Tim Tebow seeing spot duty in 2006 and then becoming larger than life in 2008. Florida won an even 100 games for the decade. LSU went 99-31, shared the 2003 title with USC under Nick Saban and won the 2007 title under Les Miles. Georgia won 98 games and had three Top 10 finishes.

National titles: 2011, 2012, 2015, 2017

Overall record: 124-15 (69-11 in the SEC)

Why they are here: Alabama was ranked No. 1 in the AP poll at some point during the season every season of the decade, and was ranked no lower than No. 3 in the AP preseason poll each season. It was Nick Saban's world, and everyone was living in it. They won two titles with AJ McCarron, who threw 179 career NFL passes. They won another with Jake Coker, who threw none. The fourth title came with Jalen Hurts, but he was benched in the CFP championship. Eighty-three players were drafted in the decade, including 28 in the first round. When Alabama lost in the 2010s, it was breaking news.

Honorable mention: Clemson only lost two regular season games in the final five seasons of the decade, collecting two national championships along the way. It beat Alabama twice in the national championship game, the second by a stunning 44-16 margin. The Tigers were eye-to-eye with the Saban Machine in the second half of the decade.

Overall record: 73-9 (44-5 in the SEC)

Why they are here: The Bulldogs are the only team to win multiple national titles this decade and they finished in the top seven of the final AP poll every year. Georgia made the last five SEC Championship Games, winning three and they became the first back-to-back national title winners since Alabama in 2011-12. Georgia's 2022 title team averaged 46.6 points per game and gave up 18.8 in its five games against ranked opponents, including a 65-7 demolition of TCU in the national title game.

Honorable mentions: Ohio State reached two national title games, winning one and is 66-11. Alabama also reached two national title games, winning one, and had four top-five AP finishes in six years.

title: Celtic boss O'Neill 'much better' after hospital procedure
description: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill revealed on Thursday he is feeling "much better" after being forced to miss last weekend's win at Kilmarnock following a hospital procedure.O'Neill was away from the Celtic squad for several days as a result of the "small" procedure.
fullText:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill revealed on Thursday he is feeling "much better" after being forced to miss last weekend's win at Kilmarnock following a hospital procedure.

O'Neill was away from the Celtic squad for several days as a result of the "small" procedure.

The 74-year-old spent a night in hospital and was unable to attend the Scottish champions' 5-1 victory over Kilmarnock on Sunday, although he did deliver a pre-match team-talk at the players' hotel.

Asked how he was feeling, the former Republic of Ireland manager told Celtic's website: "Much better, than last week anyway. Yeah, a couple of ailments rolled into one, unfortunately, but I'm getting there, which is good news."

O'Neill led Celtic to the Scottish title and the Scottish Cup last season in his second of two spells as interim boss during a turbulent campaign for the Glasgow club.

Aiming for a 15th title in the last 16 seasons, Celtic have been criticised by their fans for a lack of spending on new signings.

But O'Neill has a third recruit since the end of last season following the arrival on Wednesday of Egypt winger Haissem Hassan from Spanish side Real Oviedo.

"We'd been tracking him in January time. We have been chasing him, a number of players, in that sort of position that we feel as if they will add something to us. And he very, very much fitted the bill," O'Neill said.

"When he gets to see the surrounds here, I just think he'll glow. Going past players now is a sort of a dying art, which is really almost unforgivable in football. That's what fans get excited."

title: Watch: Freddie Freeman falls down Royals dugout steps, Dodgers 'dodge' bullet
description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.
fullText:
Aug. 13 (UPI) -- Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.

The tumble occurred in the top of the eighth inning of the 4-2 victory Wednesday in Los Angeles. Freeman said he felt soreness in his knees, shoulder, hand and wrist, but did not break any bones.

"I didn't hit my head, so that was the key part," Freeman told reporters.

Freeman said he used the cold tub and was in "good spirits" during his postgame news conference. He said he is hopeful to play Thursday at Dodger Stadium.

"I'm OK," said Freeman, who said everything on his right side is sore. "This one's not my ankle, so I should be OK."

The 10-time All-Star went 1 for 2 with a walk and a strikeout in the win. The Dodgers trailed twice through the first 2 1/2 innings, with the Royals taking two one-run leads. They took a 3-2 edge off a 397-foot, two-run homer from Shohei Ohtani and never looked back. Catcher Hunter Feduccia provided insurance with a 402-foot solo shot in the fourth.

Royals pinch hitter John Rave started the eighth with a fly out to right fielder Kyle Tucker. Designated hitter Carter Jensen reached base through a fielding error in the next at-bat.

Left fielder Isaac Collins then walked to the plate with two outs. He earned a 2-1 lead in the count against Dodgers relief pitcher Landon Knack. The right-handed pitcher then tossed in a 93-mph fastball, which Collins sliced into foul territory near first base.

Freeman pursued the ball and hovered toward the dugout. He then took a long step with his left foot, but fell down the steps instead of snagging the final out of the inning. The Dodgers star, who said he was attempting to lean on the dugout fence, told reporters that he misjudged its location. Royals players and coaches checked on Freeman before he got up and left the dugout.

Pinch hitter Michal Massey struck out in the next exchange, ending the half inning.

Freeman, who was set to lead off the bottom of the eighth, was replaced by Tommy Edman. The 17-year veteran said he experienced a similar fall about 10 years ago.

"I think that we really dodged a bullet," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Very scary visually. ... For right now, he's in good spirits, which I think is a good sign. Just kind of total body soreness. He'll be day-to-day."

Shohei flips the script! pic.twitter.com/eVrqvcBmMs— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) August 13, 2026

Freeman already was set to have Friday off. He said he did not undergo X-ray scans Wednesday night. Roberts said he doesn't plan to promote an minor league players in the wake of Freeman's fall.

Ohtani went 2 for 4 with two RBIs, a run scored and a strikeout. Shortstop Mookie Betts also homered in the victory. Dodgers starter Eric Lauer allowed four hits and two runs, including one earned, over 6 1/3 innings to improve to 7-6 this season.

Freeman hit a team-high .306 with 15 home runs and 57 RBIs through 118 games this season.

The Dodgers (73-48), who were on a seven-game losing skid earlier this month, are now on a three-game winning streak. They hold an 8.5-game lead on the San Diego Padres (65-57), who sit in second place in the National League West.

The Dodgers will host the Milwaukee Brewers, who own the best record in the National League (74-47), at 10:10 p.m. EDT Thursday in Los Angeles.

title: Bears have what they need to tread water while Luther Burden is out
description: The Bears are expected to be without Luther Burden at least through the preseason. But they have what they need to tread water while he's sidelined.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears are going to be without wide receiver Luther Burden III for the entire preseason, which leaves them down a top wideout. Head coach Ben Johnson said he's hopeful Burden will be back in time for Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers, but there's no definitive return.

Burden suffered a groin injury, which can be tough for a receiver, or any offensive playmaker for that matter, especially one with his elusive skillset. He's a big loss for Chicago's offense if he misses significant time.

With that said, the Bears offense won't be without playmakers if Burden is out of the lineup. There are plenty of weapons around to help them tread water while he is away. That starts with Rome Odunze, who's in line to be the team's top receiver.

Chicago selected Odunze with the ninth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft for that reason. He's had an up-and-down start to his career, but now is his time to shine. Odunze played extremely well to start the 2025 season, his second in the NFL, but a lingering foot injury sidelined him and impacted his play for the duration. If he can stay healthy for an entire season, the tools are there for him to be a 1,000-yard receiver with double-digit touchdowns.

Other receivers like Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, and Jahdae Walker are also there to help support. Any one of them could break out alongside Odunze while Burden is out, making them even more dangerous when he returns.

Johnson, regardless of what heights the passing attack gets to, will rely heavily on the run game as well. He loved running the ball as the play-caller in Detroit, and he loved it in his first year in Chicago. Expect big things from D'Andre Swift again with great support from Kyle Monangai.

The true X-factor here is the tight end room. Colston Loveland looks like he may be a top-five player at the position, even though the training wheels didn't come off until the second half of the 2025 season, and he then turned into a star. Cole Kmet is also a very good player who plays the position very differently. Kmet will accept any assignment given to him, while Loveland likes to line up and run routes like a true receiver on every play.

As good of a duo as Loveland and Kmet may be, there is a third name in the mix. The Bears selected Sam Roush in the 2026 NFL Draft because Johnson loves running 13-personnel. These type of plays may become commonplace if Burden misses extended time in the regular season.

Even if Burden can come back earlier than expected, with all of the weapons that Johnson has at his disposal, it may be wise to get him back to 100% health before letting him return. There is no reason to rush Burden back ahead of schedule at this point in time. They can get by without him if they need to. It isn't ideal, but the pieces are there.
