title: Only wins can stop curfew hokey-cokey for England's 'grown adults'
description: England have scrapped their midnight curfew seven months after introducing it. Now, only wins will repair the reputational damage they have sustained, says Stephan Shemilt.
fullText:
"We are grown men and we know how to behave," said Joe Root.

"As an international cricketer you are always representing the badge. We are a group of adults and we feel we can be treated like that."

Root did not say these words in 2026, but in his first stint as England captain in 2017.

It was the eve of an Ashes tour, one on which Root was without Ben Stokes because of the incident outside a Bristol nightclub.

The trip to Australia included the Jonny Bairstow-Cameron Bancroft 'headbutt' and Ben Duckett tipping a drink over James Anderson. The low point was Moeen Ali, a practising Muslim, being asked by a local journalist if he and the rest of the England players would be able to "stay out of the pub".

The midnight curfew imposed on that tour lasted more than four years until it was banished in 2022.

What is it about an away Ashes that drives Englishmen to drink? Trouble on the latest trip resulted in the return of the curfew in January yet, seven months later, Root's comeback as captain has seen the curfew, erm, put to bed.

Goodness knows what it says about the state of the England men's team that the subject of 'when grown men should go to bed' has been live for almost a decade.

You can be forgiven for struggling to keep up with England's hokey-cokey over the curfew in the past few months.

As a quick recap, rules that were introduced to the white-ball team in January were kept in place for the Test side at the beginning of the home summer.

After the first Test, captain Stokes and Gus Atkinson broke the curfew. Director of cricket Rob Key, fed up after a winter of misdemeanours, floated the idea of a total alcohol ban, while also admitting Atkinson didn't know the curfew was in place.

Head coach Brendon McCullum conceded there was some "ambiguity" around the regulations at the same time Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of any wrongdoing. Stokes came back, then retired.

Last month, England issued new guidelines to players, with the curfew still in place and advice for alcohol not to be drunk on the days immediately before, during, or immediately after a match.

England scrap midnight curfew after seven months

Then McCullum was sacked as Test coach. His last act in charge of both the Test and white-ball teams was to relax the drinking guidelines so England's T20 side could celebrate their series win against India.

Now the curfew is gone, under the instruction of Root and McCullum's replacement as Test coach - his great mate Stephen Fleming.

The England and Wales Cricket Board see Fleming as a grown-up, and he has made a grown-up move, one that also includes the curfew being lifted from a white-ball team still led by McCullum and Harry Brook.

McCullum is said to be supportive of players taking responsibility for their behaviour, which begs the question as to why he went along with the curfew in the first place.

Perhaps this is not a problem specific to this group of England players. Last week, Stokes rejected the idea that England have a drinking culture, instead suggesting the whole game has an unhealthy relationship with alcohol.

And that is not to say it is a crime every time a beer touches the lips of a cricketer.

In 2022, when England stunned New Zealand at Trent Bridge to give birth to the Bazball movement, the players celebrated on the dressing room balcony with a few drinks, then kicked on into the early hours and the Mega Munch takeaway in Nottingham.

After the Ashes of 2005, probably England's greatest series win, celebrations were led by a swaying Andrew Flintoff on an open-top bus through the streets of London.

Even this past winter, there's a decent chance Travis Head put away more than the England players. It's just that Head was scoring runs and Australia were winning.

Former cricketers will argue that any drinking taking place now is nothing worse than what was consumed in years gone by - Ian Botham, Allan Lamb, Phil Tufnell and the rest.

But perhaps that's exactly the point. Cricket has not moved with the times. You wouldn't catch famous Arsenal swillers Paul Merson and Tony Adams saying Declan Rice and Viktor Gyokeres could match them drink for drink.

It is also not fair to pin a drinking culture only on elite players. Cricket has a relationship with alcohol right down to the grassroots of the game.

I play league cricket (badly), mainly as an excuse to have a few beers.

On a Saturday, I couldn't really ask my partner to look after our two children just so I can go to the pub with 10 of my mates. Instead, I have to keep up the pretence of trying to score runs and catching the ball as a wicketkeeper. The cricket is a hindrance to getting to the bar.

Not that cricket will be too different to other amateur sports - back to the pub after Sunday league football, meeting in the bar at the tennis club, drinking games after a rugby match.

Has cricket kept up with the professional versions of those sports? Very much open to debate.

But these wider problems of the entire game are not an excuse for an England team who, frankly, would be given a pass for endless hours after midnight if they were winning.

Trouble is, they aren't, with only two victories in their past 10 Tests. The reputational damage that has been suffered over the past year will only be fixed by success on the field.

The first opportunity to start putting things right comes with three matches against Pakistan, beginning next week. After that, England's Test future is about as tough as it gets, with the major series coming away to world champions South Africa this winter, a home Ashes against Australia next summer, then five Tests in India in early 2028.

Does lifting the curfew enhance their chance of winning those series? Maybe treating the players like grown-ups off the field helps on it.

"If you want guys to take responsibility on the field, they've got to feel like they can be grown adults off it and make good, strong decisions off it," said Root on Wednesday.

Either way, England must decide their stance and stick to it. Much like constantly changing an opening pair does little for the team's output of runs, flip-flopping on rules around behaviour does not create a winning environment.

Curfew or no curfew, England can only rebuild on the field, not in the bar.

Win Tests, series and trophies, then they can go to bed as late as they please.

Rams star names 49ers nightmare he ‘hates’ facing
description: “There’s nobody that covers that much space,” Nacua said. “It’s scary. The middle of the field is terrible.”
fullText:
Puka Nacua has spent three NFL seasons tormenting defensive backs, but one San Francisco 49ers star apparently makes him reconsider the wisdom of crossing routes.

During an appearance on Logan Paul and Mike Majlak's "Impaulsive" podcast, the Los Angeles Rams receiver named Fred Warner the best defender he has faced — and said the middle of the field was akin to Warner's private haunted house.

"There's nobody that covers that much space," Nacua said. "It's scary. The middle of the field is terrible."

Nacua recalled running a route without receiving the ball, only to discover Warner waiting beside him with an explanation.

"He's like, 'I knew exactly where you're going,'" Nacua said. "Dude, I swear, when I started the play, you're on the left sideline, and now you're right here standing next to me."

Warner's response was not especially comforting: "That's just what I do."

Most linebackers pursue receivers. Warner apparently materializes beside them.

The four-time All-Pro's combination of speed, anticipation and coverage ability has made him the NFL's premier linebacker. Coaches and executives recently ranked Warner first at the position despite a broken and dislocated ankle limiting him to six games last season.

Nacua's fear comes with an important disclaimer: Warner has not exactly ruined his NFC West experience.

Across four games with Warner on the field, Nacua caught 34 of 43 targets for 357 yards and two touchdowns. Warner was credited as Nacua's primary defender on only two of those targets, allowing one seven-yard reception.

So Nacua has shredded the 49ers collectively while largely avoiding a direct appointment with the monster in the middle.

The rivalry also contains an awkward personal connection. Warner played at BYU with Nacua's older brother, Kai, leaving Puka caught between family familiarity and divisional obligation.

"Fred, I kind of hate you," Nacua recalled telling Warner. "We're supposed to not like each other, but I also enjoy watching you play."

That sounds less like trash talk and more like a frightened Yelp review: "Terrible experience. Five stars. Would reluctantly cross the middle again."

The two stars could renew their rivalry when the 49ers and Rams open the season in Melbourne. Warner is healthy and participating fully in training camp, while Nacua recently left a joint practice with minor groin soreness.

Nacua could also face NFL discipline stemming from offseason allegations, although the league has not announced a decision. His attorney has denied the claims against him.

If Nacua plays, San Francisco will again face one of the league's most productive receivers. He led the NFL with 129 receptions and 10 receiving touchdowns last season while finishing second with 1,715 yards.

Those numbers suggest Nacua is not afraid of much.

But when he enters Warner's territory, he apparently checks beneath the bed — and on both sidelines — before running his route.

title: Padres win 4-3 in 11 innings to sweep MLB-leading Brewers
description: Jackson Merrill hit a tying sacrifice fly in the 11th inning and Luis Campusano followed with a two-out single to bring in Sun-Mung Song from second base as the San Diego Padres beat the MLB-leading Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 on Wednesday for a three-game sweep.  The surging Padres have won five straight and 15 of 19 to move into the National League's second wild-card spot ahead of Arizona and Philadelphia.  Gary Sánchez doubled home the go-ahead run for Milwaukee off Adrian Morejon (9-2) in the top of the 11th.
fullText:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Jackson Merrill hit a tying sacrifice fly in the 11th inning and Luis Campusano followed with a two-out single to bring in Sun-Mung Song from second base as the San Diego Padres beat the MLB-leading Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 on Wednesday for a three-game sweep.

The surging Padres have won five straight and 15 of 19 to move into the National League's second wild-card spot ahead of Arizona and Philadelphia.

Gary Sánchez doubled home the go-ahead run for Milwaukee off Adrian Morejon (9-2) in the top of the 11th.

Merrill tied it when his sac fly off Antonio Senzatela (9-4) brought in automatic runner Jake Cronenworth. Song, who pinch ran after Ty France was hit by a pitch, stole second before Campusano punched an opposite-field single to right. Luis Lara's throw home was high, allowing Song to slide in headfirst with the winning run.

The Padres tied the game at 2 with two outs in the eighth when Fernando Tatis Jr. raced around from second base to score on Cronenworth's infield single.

Cronenworth hit a bouncer to first baseman Jake Bauers, who flipped it to reliever Aaron Ashby but he was late covering first and Cronenworth beat him to the bag for an RBI single. Ashby turned toward home but didn't make a throw as Tatis sprinted in with the tying run.

Dustin May pitched brilliantly into the eighth for the Brewers. He allowed one run and four hits, struck out six and walked two. He gave up Xander Bogaerts' homer in the third.

Sánchez, who was with the Padres for part of the 2023 season, homered to left field against Robbie Ray in the second.

Brewers LHP Shane Drohan (6-4, 3.87 ERA) is scheduled to start opposite Dodgers RHP Roki Sasaki (5-5, 4.54) on Thursday in the opener of a four-game series in Los Angeles.

Padres RHP Michael King (7-8, 3.37 ERA) is set to start Friday in the opener of a three-game series at Cleveland, which counters with RHP Gavin Williams (11-6, 3.55).

title: Lions QB Josh Dobbs 'frustrated' with how Patriots handled release
description: Detroit Lions quarterback Josh Dobbs was not happy with how he was released by the New England Patriots.
fullText:
Detroit Lions quarterback Josh Dobbs is not happy with the way that the New England Patriots handled his release from the team.

The biggest gripe for the veteran signal-caller was the timing of the release.

It came nearly two weeks after free agency, putting Dobbs in a tough spot on the open market. He missed the initial rush of the free agency period, and an argument could be made that it might have limited his opportunities.

"It was a weird offseason because it was my first time not having OTAs and everything, and that was just by the nature of my situation in New England, with the timing. That was very frustrating, the way they handled that," Dobbs said, via Pro Football Talk's Michael David Smith.

Dobbs eventually agreed to a one-year deal with the Lions on Sunday.

Timing aside, the Patriots probably don't feel bad about their decision to move forward with Tommy DeVito as the top backup quarterback behind Drake Maye. DeVito has had an impressive training camp in his second year in Josh McDaniels' offense.

The Patriots also have a young prospect developing behind the scenes with rookie sixth-round pick Behren Morton.

As for Dobbs, he will now try to make up for lost time in Detroit, where Jared Goff is the starting quarterback and Luke Altmeyer is the young prospect in training.

fullText:
While the full NBA schedule for the upcoming season hasn't been released yet, some matchups have been leaked. In the past three years, both the semifinal and final rounds took place in Las Vegas.

title: WNBA condemns 'bad-faith' actors amid discussion of transgender athletes, online hate after task force meeting
description: "There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."
fullText:
The WNBA spoke out about the "bad-faith" actors who have been dominating the discussion surrounding transgender athletes and online hate after a task force meeting on Wednesday.

WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert, team presidents and general managers met Wednesday at a previously scheduled meeting and addressed both topics among others.

"Today's meeting covered a wide range of topics, including ongoing discussions on transgender athletes and the continued hate and vitriol directed at players online," the league said through a spokesperson. "We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months. We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league.

"There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."

A statement from a WNBA spokesperson on today's task force meeting, including discussions on transgender athlete participation and the online discourse. pic.twitter.com/VVzRHbh7XO

There are no transgender players in the WNBA or preparing to enter the WNBA. The CBA also states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

Despite those facts, transgender athletes have been a large topic of discussion around the league in recent weeks after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham spoke out on the topic in an ESPN feature. She supported barring transgender athletes from women's sports, which led to anti-trans protests outside of Fever away games and an incident between a Seattle Storm minority owner and two Cunningham fans.

Naturally, the topic of transgender athletes in the WNBA has spread like wildfire on social media and elsewhere ever since. It's something that's been co-opted by more than one former men's professional basketball player, too. Many within the WNBA, including Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, have spoken out about the importance of inclusion. Reeve even wore a shirt that read, "Trans Kids Belong" during a game against the Fever.

"[The league will] always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league," Engelbert said in a memo to teams on Friday. "Second, our player eligibility rules, unlike the eligibility rules of some other leagues and governing bodies, are collectively bargained. Lastly, preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league's highest priorities.

"We recognize that this is a complex and nuanced topic, and we will continue to have important conversations with all of you and the Players Association in the weeks and months ahead."

The players association also issued a statement last Friday condemning recent hate and abuse.

"We embrace justice equity, diversity, and inclusion," the WNBPA said. "Those are the values that unite this Union and allow it to protect women's sports while creating transformational change. Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm. We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns."

Tanner Benedict returns ten players on his offense and nine on his defense from a 12-1 […]
fullText:
EL PASO, Ill. (WMBD/WYZZ) -- Could this be a state championship season in El Paso?

The El Paso-Gridley Titans were one victory away from playing in the state title game a year ago and have big expectations this fall.

Tanner Benedict returns ten players on his offense and nine on his defense from a 12-1 team that advanced to the class 2A state semifinals.

Benedict's teams are 36-17 and have been the playoffs every year since he was named head coach in 2021. But the Titans had not won a playoff game in that five-year stretch.

"Every year before last year, we had first round exits in the playoffs. The playoffs have been our Kryptonite," said senior receiver Javion Maxon. "Last year will help us this year because now we know the expectations."

Maxon is back after missing the final seven games of the season with a foot injury. Cha'von Maxon and Braden Gibson give the Titans three standout receivers who caught 25 touchdown passes last season.

All-state quarterback Owen Adams returns to lead the potent EPG offense. He threw for over 2,100 yards and 31 touchdowns last season.

The defense, led by senior defensive end Harlin Toillion, surrendered just 11 points a game last fall. The Titans are loaded and hoping they earn a trip to the state title game in late November.

"With how far we went with a young team last year, it just gives us a lot of motivation for this year," said Gibson. "We want a big win at the end of the year, near Thanksgiving."

title: Russell Westbrook's ex-teammate believes Thunder should retire jersey, build statue
description: Russell Westbrook's ex-teammate believes Oklahoma City Thunder should retire jersey, build statue.
fullText:
Once the tears were wiped away and the emotional gut punch leveled down, Oklahoma City Thunder fans quickly moved on to a pair of million-dollar questions — when will Russell Westbrook get his No. 0 jersey retired and a statue sculpted out of him?

Westbrook called it a career on Wednesday. He officially announced his retirement from the NBA after 18 seasons. Even if you're his biggest hater, the 37-year-old is universally viewed as a first-ballot Hall-of-Famer. There will be little suspense when he becomes eligible to join the prestigious club.

Even if the latter half of his career turned into a journeyman role, Westbrook will be remembered for what he did at the front nine. He spent 11 seasons on the Thunder from 2008-19. In that time, he co-starred with Kevin Durant in OKC's first title contender.

That's when Westbrook turned into an NBA superstar — and eventually, a global celebrity. His career resume speaks for itself. He's a one-time MVP winner, nine-time All-Star, nine-time All-NBA member, two-time scoring champion and three-time assist champion. He averaged a triple-double for four seasons — a statistical feat that had only happened once in the past 55 years by Oscar Robertson.

On a team level, the Thunder were in the title conversation throughout the 2010s. They had one NBA Finals trip and four Western Conference Finals appearances. Westbrook was one of the top NBA superstars at the peak of his powers. And according to one former teammate, he's easily garnered enough success to get the ultimate honor.

ESPN's Kendrick Perkins believes Westbrook should get his No. 0 jersey retired and a statue built. The two were teammates on the Thunder for four-and-a-half seasons from 2011-15. Even though he occasionally drums up some spicy opinions, the one-time NBA champion received unanimous praise for brainstorming his recommendations.

"Not only should he have his jersey retired in Oklahoma City, but he should have a statue out there as well," Perkins said. "Because after SGA, Russ, in my eyes, is the 2nd-greatest Thunder of all time."

Think Perkins will eventually be proven correct. As Westbrook's career entered its final legs, Thunder fans everywhere have repeated the same thought. They think it's a no-brainer to give OKC both honors. And I think so, too. Just a matter of when, not if.

Westbrook's No. 0 should join Nick Collison's No. 4 in the rafters sooner rather than later. Same with a statue. Although I think the latter would be better off waiting until OKC's new arena opens up in the 2028-29 season. Regardless of when those two things happen, Westbrook will forever be linked to his time on the Thunder.

title: Excellent size and team connectedness could carry the Rochelle Hubs to another successful season
description: All football teams emphasize “Team” and “Family”. The Rochelle Hubs certainly do, and they’ll rally around those two things again this season to carry them.
fullText:
ROCHELLE, Ill. (WTVO/WQRF) — All football teams emphasize "Team" and "Family". The Rochelle Hubs certainly do, and they'll rally around those two things again this season to carry them.

This Hubs teams feels that sense of team and family more than most do.

"I think that's the thing that separates us this year is the connectedness of the group, and so it's something that I get excited about," said head coach Kyle Kissack during a recent practice.

Kissack said that the other things that the Hubs are big on are attention to detail and effort.

"For us, it's always about energy and effort. How hard can we play? How long can we play that hard, and we've got to be tough."

In Rochelle once again, it'll be the "Wing T vs. Everybody". That hard-nosed ground-and-pound offensive style. That all starts with the 'Bigs' up front.

"I feel like we're really huge up front which is going to be a big thing for us, help move and run the ball more," said tight end/defensive end Warren Schweitzer.

"We've got both tackles coming back, me and Cobos, and then Harley, that's just, he's just a big guy," said two-way lineman Grant Daugherty.

Harley is junior Brayden Harley, 6'4 and 270 pounds if not more. For more size there's the Sweitzer brothers 6'7 Warren and 6'5 Eli. They both play at the same time much of the time at both tight end and defensive end.

"It's not often you get a big kid but get two from the same family," said Kissack. "It's something we're really excited about."

The Hubs wishbone attack did lose the point of its spear from last year. Fullback Roman Villalobos graduated. He was First Team All-State in Class 4A, and he rushed for nearly 1200 yards and 16 touchdowns.

"When those kinds of kids come through your program, they're irreplaceable," admitted Kissack.

However, the Hubs do have a good player to plug in at fullback who they're high on, junior Andrew Eyster. Kissack has a simple message for Eyster.
"We just want the best version of you. We don't want you to be somebody that you're not."

At wingback, the Hubs will have a running back by committee approach that will include Tyler Gensler, Jonathan Andrist, and Luke Chadwick. Junor Cohen Haedt returns as the starting quarterback

Gensler will be one of the leaders on defense at linebacker. Andrist and Aiden Carmichael also will play linebacker. Harley, Caiden Harris, Adam Cobos and Grant Daugherty will be on the defensive front.

For coverage of the Hubs throughout the season and high school football around the 815, watch "Overtime" Friday nights on FOX 39 in Rockford.

title: Hometown hero Hudson-Smith basks in Euro glory
description: Hometown hero Matthew Hudson-Smith enjoyed a dream return to the Birmingham track where he started out as a nine-year-old by regaining his European 400m title on Wednesday.It was a fifth European gold for Hudson-Smith, taking him level with 400m runner Roger Black and distance great Mo Farah.
fullText:
Hometown hero Matthew Hudson-Smith enjoyed a dream return to the Birmingham track where he started out as a nine-year-old by regaining his European 400m title on Wednesday.

The 31-year-old, who had won the one-lap race at European championships in Berlin 2018 and Munich in 2022, said "nobody was going to beat me on this track".

Hudson-Smith, born in neighbouring Wolverhampton in England's West Midlands, even had a temporary stand at the Alexander Stadium for these championships named after him.

It was a fifth European gold for Hudson-Smith, taking him level with 400m runner Roger Black and distance great Mo Farah. He is just one behind Dina Asher-Smith in terms of British athletes.

Setting off quickly, the Briton had the 14,000-strong crowd on their feet as he clocked 44.17 seconds for victory, 0.23sec ahead of France's Muhammad Abdallah Kounta, who is coached by British sprint legend Linford Christie.

Dutch athlete Jonas Phijffers took bronze in a national record of 44.41.

"My coach told me 'This is your home -- defend it'. I knew that for them to beat me they have to have a super special moment," said Hudson-Smith.

"Nobody was going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I have been here since nine."

There were three other medal events in an entertaining evening session.

Switzerland's Jason Joseph won the 110m hurdles in 13.12 seconds in the final event, eliciting a sustained peal of cowbell ringing from a large Swiss contingent in the crowd.

France's Just Kwaou-Mathey took silver in 13.16sec and Poland's Jakub Szymanski bronze (13.26).

- Zapletalova fills Bol's shoes -

In-form Slovakian Emma Zapletalova filled the void left in the 400m hurdles by two-time world and European champion Femke Broeders-Bol with a dominant victory in 52.91 seconds.

Broeders-Bol has opted to transition into the 800m, leaving the field wide open.

Zapletalova, who won a bronze medal behind Broeders-Bol at last year's Tokyo world champs, led home Britain's Emily Newnham.

Newnham clocked a personal best of 53.33sec, with Fatoumata Binta Diallo of Portugal taking bronze in a national record of 53.55sec.

Silja Kosonen ensured Finland's first-ever medal in the women's hammer throw with victory with a best of 76.28 metres.

Kosonen, a former world under-20 champion who has placed fifth and fourth at the last two senior championships, threw her best on her third effort and never looked like being under real pressure from that moment.

Defending champion Sara Fantini of Italy claimed silver with 74.35, while Norway's Beatrice Nedberge Llano rounded out the podium (72.88).

Britain could also dream of more sprint glory as newly-crowned 100m champion Amy Hunt, Dina Asher-Smith and Success Eduan all qualified for Thursday's final, scheduled for 2048 GMT.

Hunt coasted her semi-final in 22.37sec, while 2019 world champion and two-time European gold medallist Asher-Smith, fifth in the 100m final, won her semi in 22.49sec.

"The plan today was to come out and put down a hard first 150m, in order to practice it for tomorrow," said Hunt, who is aiming for four championship golds as she also plans to compete in both the women's and mixed 4x100m relays.

"I felt so strong from the turn and was just trying to look at the screen seeing where I was, what the time was."

Swiss defending champion Mujinga Kambundji, on the road back from becoming a new mother, will miss the final after coming in seventh in that semi, raising hopes further of a British cleansweep of the podium.

"It's amazing to have three British girls in the final," said Eduan.

"Me, Amy and Dina haven't actually spoken about the possible cleansweep. We all just want to focus on our own races, but it would be amazing if that did happen."

title: Esteban Ribovics has different kind of bonus in mind for UFC 330
description: Esteban Ribovics wants to put on a show against Edson Barbosa at UFC 330 but not the type fans would expect.
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA – Esteban Ribovics wants a bonus at UFC 330, but not the type he's been getting through his UFC run.

Ribovics (15-3 MMA, 4-3 UFC), who's quickly become a fan-favorite lightweight, takes on fellow exciting striker Edson Barboza (24-14 MMA, 18-14 UFC) on the preliminary card of UFC 330 (Paramount+) – which takes place Saturday at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. Many are already pitting the matchup as a potential Fight of the Night for the card, as Ribovics has won three of those bonuses in his last four fights and Barboza has won 10 in his UFC career.

Ribovics enjoys the reputation he's built and wants to put on a show, but one that involves him winning a bonus in a different style.

"Winning the bonuses has helped me a ton, especially having won them in a consecutive manner," Ribovics said in Spanish at UFC 330 media day. "It's helped me economically and also got me the name of someone who's violent and goes out there to put in wars. I think it motivates me to get another one, but this time I don't want Fight of the Night. I want Performance of the Night. I also haven't won a $100,000 one. I want to win one."

The Ribovics-Barboza matchup pairs two exciting strikers from different generations. Ribovics is 10 years younger than Barboza and has 20 fights fewer than the Brazilian. To some, this might have been an improbable matchup, given the generational gap between the two, but not for Ribovics.

"Yeah, I actually did think this fight could happen," Ribovics said. "Once you're in the UFC, you expect to run into these fights. There's a saying I like that says, 'Train so hard until your idols become your rivals,' and that's what's happening. He was a guy, and still is a guy I respect a lot and I admire due to his trajectory, but he's also just another guy in front of me."

title: NBA on NBC schedules first ever Presidents Day quadrupleheader
description: Christmas Day has been the traditional home for the NBA’s marquee regular season showcase event. But with the NFL now encroaching on their territory, the league is expanding its offering on other holidays. And in a brand new move, one of those holidays just happens to be the day after Super Bowl LXI. NBC has…
fullText:
Christmas Day has been the traditional home for the NBA's marquee regular season showcase event. But with the NFL now encroaching on their territory, the league is expanding its offering on other holidays.

And in a brand new move, one of those holidays just happens to be the day after Super Bowl LXI.

NBC has announced that the network will all four games for the first-ever Presidents Day quadrupleheader on February 15, 2027.

The lineup is headlined by some of the teams that the NBA will showcase on Christmas Day and Opening Night, but with some intriguing storylines added in.

It starts with LaMelo Ball and the Timberwolves visiting Charlotte in his first visit back to his former home. Then, LeBron James is featured once again, this time against former teammate Kyrie Irving, Cooper Flagg, and the Mavericks. The mouth-watering matchup between Victor Wembanyama and Giannis Antetokounmpo is the feature attraction at 5 p.m. ET with the Spurs facing the Heat. Finally, the nightcap will see the Indiana Pacers play the Golden State Warriors with a duel of Tyrese Haliburton and Steph Curry.

It's a forward thinking move from the NBA. Why not go all-in on a holiday that can literally take the ball from the NFL the day after the Super Bowl? It also helps that it's the middle of winter and lots of people throughout the country will be inside.

Additionally, NBC will have the Martin Luther King Jr. Day quadruple-header that has seen more emphasis from the NBA in recent years. That full lineup consists of Pistons-Cavs, Sixers-Hawks, Timberwolves-Knicks, and Rockets-Grizzlies. It's no coincidence that the only team to feature on all four premier national showcase occasions is LeBron James and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

For both doubleheaders, NBC and Peacock will carry games at 12 p.m. ET, 2:30 p.m. ET, and 5 p.m. ET. The last game in both sets will be at 7:30 p.m. ET and feature mainly on Peacock, but will also on linear television through NBCSN.

title: UFC 330’s Mansur Abdul-Malik reflects on first professional loss – ‘I was trying to be perfect’
description: “Perfection is not attainable, but if we chase perfection we can catch excellence.” – Vince Lombardi Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Middleweight prospect Mansur Abdul-Malik returns to action against Dustin Stoltzfus on the UFC 330 main card this weekend (Sat., Aug. 15, 2026) inside Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Abdul-Malik is coming off the first […]
fullText:
"Perfection is not attainable, but if we chase perfection we can catch excellence." – Vince Lombardi

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Middleweight prospect Mansur Abdul-Malik returns to action against Dustin Stoltzfus on the UFC 330 main card this weekend (Sat., Aug. 15, 2026) inside Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

Abdul-Malik is coming off the first loss of his professional career, suffering a third-round stoppage against Yousri Belgaroui in a brutal fight at UFC Seattle (watch highlights).

When fighters lose their undefeated records, many admit to feeling relieved that the pressure of protecting the "0" is finally gone. Others respond by completely overhauling their training and lifestyle.

The 28-year-old Las Vegas-based fighter initially felt the urge to change everything after the loss. However, once he took an honest look at his life, he realized there was not much away from the cage that needed fixing.

"Maybe early on after the fight happened, of course, the mental perspective makes you want to change everything—change your lifestyle, change your habits," Abdul-Malik told reporters during UFC 330 media day. "But then I look at my lifestyle and habits, and I'm like, 'What is there really to change?' I don't party, I don't drink, I don't go out and I don't have many friends, so it's like, what is there to change?

"The thing to change was to be myself," Abdul-Malik continued. "I was going out there trying to be way too perfect, and there are a lot of flaws in trying to be perfect."

Instead of reinventing himself following his first defeat, Abdul-Malik wants to rediscover the aggressive, playful fighter who helped him emerge as one of the division's most intriguing prospects.

"My intention is to go out there and be me and fight like me," Abdul-Malik said. "To be aggressive, to be playful and have a smile on my face—I felt like I was way too serious, if anything. But all those things are secondary. I lost to a fighter who was better than me. Period. Point blank."

"Now, I have an opportunity to just perform, man," he concluded. "Perform, be myself, have fun and engage."

Armed with that rock-solid mentality, Abdul-Malik will look to stop Stoltzfus, who has trained at Xtreme Couture several times over the past few years and should be familiar with his opponent's surroundings.

Abdul-Malik is currently 3-1-1 inside the Octagon with three finishes. He also owns a 100 percent career finishing rate, with all seven of his professional wins coming by knockout.

Now, the once-unbeaten prospect gets his first opportunity to show how he responds to adversity

title: Former NFL QB Matt Hasselbeck part of latest CTE frontier — diagnosing brain disease in the living
description: Former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck has participated in a study at Boston University to find ways to diagnose chronic traumatic encephalopathy in living individuals.
fullText:
Matt Hasselbeck took some nasty hits to the head during his 17-year NFL career, four years at Boston College and a childhood full of sports, but the quarterback seems to have emerged from more than two decades of collisions relatively unscathed, enjoying middle adulthood with his wife and three children.

The 50-year-old knows that some of his friends and former teammates haven't been as lucky.

That's why the three-time Pro Bowl selection recently spent two days at Boston University, going through a battery of scans and tests to determine how much all those collisions affected his brain. The hope is that it will be a small step toward a goal that has eluded doctors — diagnosing chronic traumatic encephalopathy in the living.

"They need guys like me — they need people who are feeling good to step up to the plate and volunteer," Hasselbeck said. "I played quarterback, so I didn't take some of the hits that a lot of my teammates took.

"But the guys who were blocking for me, or playing special teams, or trying to get the ball back for me on defense, I wanted to do something. They had my back, so in a way I'd like to have their back."

A degenerative brain disease that has been linked to concussions and other head trauma common in military combat and contact sports, CTE has been diagnosed in more than 100 former NFL players, casting a pall over the United States' most popular sports league. Some high-profile football players diagnosed with CTE after their deaths include Hall of Famers like linebacker Junior Seau and quarterback Ken Stabler, along with former Patriots tight end Aaron Hernandez.

Right now, CTE can only be diagnosed after death.

CTE can affect regions of the brain involved with regulating behavior and emotions. This can lead to memory loss, depression, violent mood swings and other cognitive and behavioral issues, though researchers note these symptoms can also be linked to other illnesses.

Hasselbeck's participation is just a small part of a study that Michael Alosco, co-director of clinical research at the Boston University CTE Center, hopes will expand to hundreds of participants in multiple locations. Alosco is the principal investigator in Boston and there are also sites in California, Arizona, Texas and Florida with potentially more to come.

The study seeks two types of people: Those who played professional or college football and those who have been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and never played contact or collision sports and have no history of repetitive head impacts.

Alosco said there are many similarities between Alzheimer's and CTE because both are degenerative brain diseases, but there are also some key differences, and mapping out those discrepancies is key to figuring out a way to diagnose CTE properly.

"We've applied what we've known worked for Alzheimer's disease, but we've learned it does not work for CTE," Alosco said. "We've really got to push discovery efforts and find the marker that's specific to the protein of CTE versus Alzheimer's because they're different.

"How we're going to get there is through the research we're doing right now."

Nicholas Ashton, the principal investigator in Phoenix, said roughly 10 patients have participated at the Arizona site. He said that currently, diagnosing CTE in the living is mostly guesswork because so many of the symptoms mimic Alzheimer's.

"The more people involved, the more information we get and the closer we get to an answer," Ashton said. "Treatments exploded with Alzheimer's once we were able to accurately diagnose. We're trying to get to the same spot with CTE."

Hasselbeck said he went through a variety of mental tests — like counting backward from 100 by sevens and reciting the alphabet backward. He also had a blood sample taken, an MRI on his brain and a PET (positron emission tomography) scan that injects a small amount of safe radioactive tracer that maps out the brain's function.

The former quarterback said the procedures were eye-opening and humbling.

"I've got a healthy respect for people who are dealing with serious brain trauma, whether it's tumors or cancer," Hasselbeck said. "I walked in there feeling completely healthy and you still get a little anxious when you're doing a brain scan, an MRI. You come out and you're looking at your brain."

Hasselbeck is also donating his brain for research after he dies.

Not everyone in the study is a famous former NFL player.

Bryan Savage, a 56-year-old who lives in Maryland, is a former linebacker at Union College in Schenectady, New York — an NCAA Division III school. He traveled to Boston for the study and also has committed to donating his brain.

Savage said he's lucky to be relatively healthy but that he's been diagnosed with depression and ADHD over the past few years.

"I was interested because of some of the things that I've gone through physically and mentally," Savage said. "You wonder if it's just getting older, a midlife crisis or if it's related to any brain trauma I might have had playing football."

Savage praised the researchers who were with him during the study and said he was relieved to find out his brain scans look normal for a man in his mid-50s. He's reached out to some of his former teammates, encouraging them to get involved in the study.

"I'll talk to some of my former friends and they're going through a lot of the same things," Savage said. "They'll say — 'Why do I feel like this? I've never been depressed. Things that I used to be passionate about I don't care about anymore.'"

Alosco said the main reason Alzheimer's research is much more advanced than CTE research is sheer numbers: Alzheimer's research dates back decades and there have been countless people who have been studied.

"The (Alzheimer's progress) is through years and years of research, of people donating their brains, and also collecting data during life," Alosco said. "While we've been studying CTE for a while, we haven't had the point where we've had all this data during life, that have also donated their brain. We need to get to that place."

He added: "I'm really hopeful about detecting CTE — I don't think that's too distant. Once we can accurately diagnose, that's when we can start some treatment trials."

Hasselbeck — who played in the NFL for the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Tennessee Titans and Indianapolis Colts — said he had three concussions before he even started college, one playing football, another on the basketball court and another while goofing around while ice skating. He had a few concussions during his college or NFL career, but he wasn't sure of the exact number because some might have gone undetected since there was a culture of toughness in locker rooms, particularly early in his career.

Hasselbeck's pro career spanned from 1998 to 2015 and the quarterback said there was a huge change regarding head injuries during that time. Early in his career, the only acceptable answer after a hit to the head was "I'm good," but by the mid 2010s, players were much more honest about potential concussions.

Hasselbeck's proud of that change. Now he hopes his participation in the current CTE study can continue that progress.

"I've always had a passion for making the game safer," Hasselbeck said. "I love football. One of the things I'm most proud of as an NFL guy is not just as a player, but the entire time I worked with the league and NFLPA for ways to make the game safer."

title: May’s flowers wilted by bullpen in Brewers 4-3 loss
description: May’s stellar outing spoiled by bullpen and offense’s lack luster production
fullText:
West Coast nightmares continue to haunt the Brewers as the San Diego Padres finish the three-game series sweep in a 4-3 extra-inning affair. The Brewers are now 4-8 on the season when playing on the West Coast.

From Dustin May's stellar seven-inning performance to the four double plays turned by the defense, followed by a bullpen blowup and some other critical mistakes, today's game was filled with a lot of ups and downs. Things didn't get off on the right foot either in the bottom of the second as Joey Ortiz mishandled a groundball to allow Luis Rengifo to reach base safely. He did make it up a play later by turning the first of four double plays.

Entering today's ballgame, the Brewers had scored just four runs all series, which is a sight for sore eyes compared to what we've seen from this team all season. With the team avoiding some major injuries a night ago, the offense needed a spark, and that's what Gary Sánchez gave to them in the top of the second inning with a solo home run to left field.

There goes El Kraken 🐙 https://t.co/UesnAWKNdG pic.twitter.com/dJzJx6ejmv

Despite the rocky defensive play all series, and the rough start from Ortiz early in the first inning, the defense felt like it finally found its groove. During the bottom of the second inning, Jackson Merrill grounded into the Padres' second straight double play to quickly give his team two outs. Quickly resulting into another 1-2-3 inning as Austin Hays grounded out shortly thereafter.

Playing in his first game since August 8, Ortiz was trying to be another man in this lineup to provide another pop, but instead of using his bat, he walked with one out in the top of the third inning. After advancing to second base on a groundout, Brice Turang drove in Ortiz with a single to extend the Brewers' lead to 2-0.

May was stellar this afternoon in his second appearance in a Brewers uniform, throwing a quick and efficient seven innings of one-run ball on just four hits and two walks, while striking out six batters. His one blemish of the game came in the bottom of the third when Xander Bogaerts hit his 10th home run of the season to cut the Brewers' lead down to 2-1.

In terms of offense, both sides were quite stale going forward. In the bottom of the fourth inning, the bases were loaded for the Padres, with one out. In dire need to get out of the inning to maintain their lead, May forced Hays into an inning-ending double play, making it the third double play grounded into by the Padres in the game.

From that point on, the Padres offense was retired in order until the bottom of the eighth inning. Pat Murphy sent May back out to the mound for his eighth inning of work, as he had thrown less than 80 pitches at that point in the ballgame. A decision that felt like a no-brainer considering the four-game series with the Dodgers looming beginning tomorrow.

Dustin May: certified Brewer pic.twitter.com/mMQIuDiufx

May came out and walked Gavin Sheets on four straight balls to open up the bottom of the eighth. Chad Patrick then replaced May, and he then forced Bogaerts into a double play, clearing all but one from the bases. Then the command issues came for Patrick as he loaded the bases on back-to-back walks. Following the second walk, Aaron Ashby came in to take things over. Brewers killer Jake Cronenworth then singled to score Fernando Tatis Jr. to tie the game at 2-2.

Nothing happened on offense for the Brewers in the top of the ninth, but the Padres continued to be pesky, and more so, Merrill continued to be pesky, as he doubled with one out. After Luis Campusano popped out for the second out of the inning, Jase Bowen lined a ball into center field, where Garrett Mitchell stretched out to take away the win for the Padres, leaving the game at 2-2.

G LAYS OUT TO KEEP US TIED pic.twitter.com/1GJ1SFfJw8

After another quiet 10th inning from both offenses, the Brewers finally broke the silence in the top of the 11th inning. Once again, it was Sánchez who came through with the clutch hit as he doubled a ball off the third base bag to score Jihwan Bae, giving the Brewers a 3-2 lead. After a Mitchell walk with no outs, David Hamilton and Ortiz followed with strikeouts of their own to quickly put the Brewers down. Padres then walked Jackson Chourio before getting Turang to strike out to end the inning, wasting valuable time to extend the Brewers' lead.

El Gary delivers in the clutch pic.twitter.com/oVc2t8Mifo

Antonio Senzatela replaced closer Trevor Megill on the bump for the bottom of the 11th inning and was out to a great start by forcing a groundout. Then, Merrill drove in the tying run with a flyout to left field that should've been more if it wasn't for Luis Lara's spectacular catch. While trying to ride high on the catch, Campusano hit a single to drive in the winning run, securing the series sweep of the Brewers.

Looking back at this series, offense was the main issue, as it feels like almost everyone is in a slump. Today, though Sánchez carried the offense, he also hurt the defensive side of the ball with several passed balls and a play at the end of the game that resulted in poor positioning. Certainly not the way the Brewers want to be feeling heading into a four-game series with the Dodgers.

Despite getting two quality starts from Logan Henderson and May, the Brewers will look to get back on track tomorrow in Los Angeles with Shane Drohan on the mound. The offense will also look to generate more runs in this next series, as against the Padres they were 2-for-24 with runners in scoring position.

Tomorrow's game will be a late one as first pitch is scheduled for 9:10 p.m., and you can find that as normal on Brewers.TV and WTMJ 620.

title: WNBA denounces 'bad-faith efforts' in statement addressing Enes Kanter, Royce White draft declarations
description: Here's what the league's anti-hate task force had to say about two former NBA players 'declaring' for the WNBA Draft
fullText:
WNBA denounces 'bad-faith efforts' in statement addressing Enes Kanter, Royce White draft declarations originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

As the WNBA has been under the spotlight regarding a handful of controversies recently, league representatives met to discuss how to move forward.

The WNBA's anti-hate task force met on Wednesday amid the league facing questions about transgender athletes while its players have been subject to online vitriol. The league has always tried to promote inclusivity, but this season has had its fair share of questionable moments.

Therefore, it's important that the league makes sure everyone is on the same page entering the home stretch of the season. Here's what the league's anti-hate task force had to say.

MORE: What WNBA rulebook says about Enes Kanter Freedom's eligibility

The WNBA released a statement on Wednesday explaining that the league's anti-hate task force met and discussed recent events.

The discussions appeared to centre on both the eligibility of transgender athletes in the league and online vitriol directed toward players. The statement also denounced "bad-faith efforts" to use these topics against the league's efforts to promote inclusivity.

The WNBA’s anti-hate task force meet today.

USA TODAY received a statement from a league spokesperson about the meeting.

Full statement: pic.twitter.com/Tebn6gv9EH

MORE:Why Sophie Cunningham doubled down on transgender athlete stance

The WNBA has been at the center of a firestorm of controversy recently that has extended beyond on-court play. Most recently, former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White have put forth their efforts to enter the WNBA draft, arguing that the league's rules towards transgender athletes make them eligible to play.

Additionally, WNBA players are consistently facing online pushback towards their on-court play or off-court opinions from both passionate and casual fans. Therefore, the league felt the need to meet to discuss how to move forward.

MORE:What to know about WNBA transgender rallies, protests

In 2025, the WNBA announced the  No Space for Hate" as it aims to fight hate both on and off the court. That included creating a task force comprised of "league and team representatives" with support from the players association.

"As the WNBA continues to grow in popularity and influence, we're proud to launch 'No Space for Hate' — a league-wide initiative to better protect players, preserve the spirit of the game, and affirm the values of our league," commissioner Cathy Engelbert said last year. "We believe that basketball can be a unifying force — a place where people from all walks of life come together not just to watch a game, but to connect,"

The WNBA's Collective Bargaining Agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," clearly stating that men are not eligible to play in the league. It doesn't have a specific article addressing the eligibility of transgender athletes, which is pretty standard among women's leagues in North America.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 6 of Cincinnati Bearcats training camp
description: Cincinnati Bearcats football training camp is into its second week. Here are five takeaways from UC beat reporter Scott Springer
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bearcats are into their second week of training camp and are coming up on three weeks away from the Nippert Stadium season opener against Boston College (Sept. 5).

Thus far, the offensive line has commanded the headlines with Preseason All-American guard Evan Tengesdahl recently making the "Freaks List" annually put out by Bruce Feldman of Fox Sports. On this Wednesday, Aug. 12, Tengesdahl added the Lombardi Watch List to his accolades.

The Lombardi Award is given to the nation's top college football lineman or linebacker who best exemplifies the character, discipline, grit, and leadership of Hall of Fame coach Vince Lombardi. Tengesdahl is one of 54 standouts selected nationwide and one of just six representatives from the Big 12.

"One of the most powerful players in college football."@EvanTengesdahl_ ➡️ 2026 @BruceFeldmanCFB Freaks List pic.twitter.com/Eq3oPGtnv7

The luxury of an indoor facility is not missing a beat in practice. In their new building, the Bearcats are just steps from their locker room to the field, while on dry days it's a short hike to Nippert Stadium.

Another reason to bypass Camp Higher Ground was also the size of the football staff. When then-coach Rick Minter started going to West Harrison, Indiana, there weren't as many coaches or support personnel. In a Power Four conference like the Big 12, there's more personnel and more effort needed to pull off a remote practice while using the same 2026 technology and sports science methods.

Most recently, the team required an additional hotel within driving distance to accommodate the extra staff. And if there was a thunderstorm, the only solution was to wait it out inside.

"This is the best I've been around facility-wise," fifth-year safety Jasper Beeler said. "The way we work here and the intensity, I haven't been able to do that at any other place. All that we have here is amazing."

Gradually, the August practices have gotten more physical. The chatter between defensive backs and receivers has been evident and the offense (white jerseys) and defense (black jerseys) have been pretty spirited this week.

Safety CJ Jones had a tremendous interception while battling for the ball with receiver Giyahni (Gio) Kontosis. Kontosis and JV Gibson have given some defensive backs fits, but Jones came away with the football.

Safety MJ Cannon also had a big goal-line play and things have been very competitive when there's a running play involved.

"I love it!" Beeler said. "It's football, man. At the end of the day, everybody wants to compete, everybody wants to win. Obviously, it's going to get physical; we're all grown men."

Beeler transferred to UC from Northern Illinois and is part of a group of safeties trying to fill the void of South Alabama transfer Ty Goodwill, who is out for the season with an Achilles injury. Goodwill sent his teammates a video shortly after getting out of surgery, asking about their progress.

At 6-foot-3 and 325 pounds, Tyo isn't afraid of much.

He raised and showed hogs as a kid and was a state meet wrestler and thrower (shot and discus) on the track team in addition to his punishing blocks. Now, he's enjoying the limelight with Tengesdahl and Joe Cotton as the "Pancake Trio", particularly when an offensive line coach a few years ago here didn't give him the time of day.

Tyo works out his frustrations on the field and likes to follow the ball after he's plowed the hole.

"I love getting down the field, blowing up piles, blowing up corners, safeties, whatever it is," Tyo said.

In the August 11 practice, it was Notre Dame transfer Gi'Bran Payne with the long touchdown run. Aug. 12, it was Zion Johnson with a few quick bursts. Johnson played late last year when Evan Pryor was sidelined and is the most experienced back in terms of being a Bearcat.

The UC backs range from 5-foot-8 to around 5-foot-10, and Johnson now has 192 pounds on his frame with good speed. Once he's through a hole, there's no turning back.

"I don't want to say nobody, but there's very few people catching me," Johnson said. "They (offensive line) are making the holes way, way bigger. They're just executing and doing their jobs. Today's practice was very physical, which was needed. From the offensive side, we just came out and wanted it."

Also getting in on the action Aug. 12 was Zylan Perry, who had a touchdown with some push from the offensive line and junior James Lewis and freshman Jayzon Thompson both had scores.

A former walk-on himself, Scott Satterfield has always enjoyed having key walk-ons. Antwan Peek Jr., came from Indian Hill as a walk-on defensive back and now is a scholarship key defender at outside linebacker. Edge rusher Drew Logan was put on scholarship last year.

At tight end, Lyviel Waters of Winton Woods has turned heads and found the end zone in the Aug. 12 practice with the entire offense running out to celebrate.

On the defensive line, Nathan Nunn is a 6-foot-2, 282-pound junior whose father is edge-rushers coach Robert Nunn. The elder Nunn has 19 years of NFL experience, including a Super Bowl win with the Giants. He's also coached NFL Hall of Famers Bruce Smith and Jason Taylor.

"One of the bright spots is Nunn," Satterfield said. "He's a guy that can play all over the D-line. He's a walk-on guy that's earned his stripes. He's going to give us some great minutes this year."

Said center Tyo, "Nunn's doing a great job. He's done a great job transforming his body and getting stronger."

Tyo also pointed out 6-foot-1, 320-pound freshman Jonathan Rulo from Belleville, Illinois, as someone to watch.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: 5 takeaways from Day 6 of Cincinnati Bearcats training camp

title: Could Chaz Coleman play again? Former Vols transfer sparks comeback speculation
description: Medically DQ'd top transfer DE Chaz Coleman showed himself training in a new social media post that has reignited questions about his football future.
fullText:
Could Chaz Coleman be making a return to the football field after being medically disqualified following a transfer to Tennessee this past offseason?

It appears it could be on the bingo card after a social media post he made Wednesday, Aug. 12.

College football's next big stars? 10 freshmen who could make instant impact in 2026

In that X post, Coleman showed four videos of himself going through drills at a gym. According to Adam Sparks of the Knoxville News Sentinel — part of the USA TODAY Network — the location is unknown, but the former Vols 6-4 defensive end is no longer with the football program or enrolled at Tennessee.

Coleman, ranked as the No. 3 edge rusher and No. 16 overall player in 247Sports' transfer rankings, was one of the Vols' top pickups in the portal this past offseason. He followed Penn State defensive coordinator Jim Knowles to Tennessee.

🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/KAXjubPE0l

He was medically disqualified in late June by the Vols. As noted by Knox News, if a player is medically disqualified, he could transfer to another school and play in a future season if they are medically cleared. They are just no longer able to play at the school where they were medically disqualified.

"Real sorry not having Chaz. I hope the best for him as a young man," Knowles said of Coleman during a Aug. 4 media availability. "(Pass rush) is kind of how Chaz made his mark last year at Penn State. We just set up opportunities for him in the game to be creative and pass rush.

"So it's a question mark (for Tennessee's 2026 defense) and time will tell how that goes. But we need to have other tools in the toolbox to create the pass rush, if need be. And we'll have that."

Coleman finished with eight tackles, one broken-up pass, one sack and one forced fumble last season at Penn State.

Tennessee is set to open the season on Saturday, Sept. 5 against Furman at 3:30 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee.

title: Hamilton West Side tops Kentucky, reaches Little League World Series
description: The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021.
fullText:
The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021 after defeating Kentucky's North Oldham, 6-0, in Whitestown, Indiana, in the Great Lakes region championship game on ESPN2.

The 2026 Little League World Series begins on Wednesday, Aug. 19, in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. As the Great Lakes region winner, West Side will face the yet-to-be-determined Mountain Region champion on Aug. 20 at 2 p.m.

West Side starter Boone Treadway, the son of Badin head coach Brion Treadway, pitched a one-hit, complete-game shutout. He threw 62 pitches, and struck out nine.

"Feels amazing," Treadway told ESPN after the game. "I'm just glad to get to do it with this group of kids."

Josiah Infante hit a two-run homer during West Side's six-run first inning.

West Side is a 23-time Ohio state champion. In 2021, West Side advanced to the LLWS final before losing to Michigan.

West Side and North Oldham met twice in the Great Lakes regional. West Side won the first meeting, 11-4.

West Side cruised past Michigan and Indiana in the first two rounds of the tournament.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Hamilton West Side tops Kentucky, reaches Little League World Series

title: Kasey Kahne is as passionate and competitive as ever at Knoxville Nationals
description: He's back in the Knoxville Nationals and looks like a legitimate contender
fullText:
This is just what Kasey Kahne does.
Racers race.

Eight years removed from his last NASCAR Cup Series race, Kasey Kahne is 46-years-old and as busy as ever.

"It's been a really good year and it's been fun because I've done a lot of things away from the racetrack and at the racetrack this year and some unexpected things," Kahne told Motorsport.com on Wednesday before his Knoxville Nationals prelim night.

For example, Kahne finally earned his elusive first victory on the World of Outlaws tour back in May at Williams Grove Speedway. He did so, not behind the wheel of the Kasey Kahne Racing No. 4, but instead the No. 39M for the injured Anthony Macri.

He's back behind the wheel in his own car this week, alongside full-time driver and teammate Daison Pursley, who took over for the legendary Brad Sweet at the end of last season.

"Being in the Macri car, that was a completely unexpected phone call," Kahne said. "And then to get to run 10 races for that strong of a team and Anthony as a driver support just helped me a ton.

"So yeah, the racing stuff's been really fun this year. I have really enjoyed myself. And then there's pushing the No. 9 guys to keep improving. I haven't raced with them a ton this year, so this feels a little different, but it's been a really enjoyable season for sure."

Kahne continues to race, and continues to own cars at this level, all because he is still as competitive as he ever was. He wants to compete in every facet of this discipline possible.

"I never lost my passion for driving," Kahne said. "I've never lost the passion being competitive as an owner. Sure, I might not be good today but we have a chance to be really good tomorrow with Daison, and I am driven to figure out all of it.

"I still have that drive to be hands on. I'm passionate and competitive. So there's not a lot stopping me right now. Luckily, Amy (Long) and (kids) Ana and Tanner are supportive of me. If they weren't, then I wouldn't do it."

title: LB Elandon Roberts returning to Pittsburgh on a one-year deal
description: Free agent linebacker Elandon Roberts is returning to Pittsburgh.
fullText:
Free agent linebacker Elandon Roberts is returning to Pittsburgh.

The Steelers reached an agreement with the 10-year veteran on a one-year deal, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

Roberts, 32, played in Pittsburgh in 2023 and 2024 before departing for Las Vegas, where he played for current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.

Roberts entered the NFL as a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2016. He played four years in New England and three in Miami before landing in Pittsburgh the first time.

In his career, Roberts has totaled 694 tackles, 14.5 sacks, 37 quarterback hits, an interception, 13 passes defensed and five forced fumbles.

title: Aaron Rodgers wanted to play at Lambeau field one last time
description: Future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers played the vast majority of his games throughout his NFL career at Lambeau Field as a member of the Green Bay Packers. Now, as he enters the final season of his storied career, he’ll never have a chance to play there again, and it sounds like he’s a…
fullText:
Future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers played the vast majority of his games throughout his NFL career at Lambeau Field as a member of the Green Bay Packers. Now, as he enters the final season of his storied career, he'll never have a chance to play there again, and it sounds like he's a little sad about it.

During a recent interview, Rodgers lamented the fact that Thursday night's preseason game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Packers is not at Lambeau Field, which would have given him one last time to play at the stadium where he played his home games for 18 seasons.

During a Zoom call with Packers reporters on Wednesday, Rodgers admitted that he wishes the upcoming preseason game had been scheduled as a road contest rather than a home game, even though returning as a visiting player would have been "strange."

"100%, 100%," Rodgers said via ESPN. "When I heard it was possible to play both my former teams, I was really hoping this one was going to be in Green Bay, not just to get back at Lambeau one more time, but to head out to Chives [restaurant] for a dinner and maybe head out to Green Bay Country Club for a quick nine or something. I was really hoping it was going to be in Green Bay for a lot of reasons.

"It would have been strange, being in that [visitors] locker room and stuff, but I would have found my way over, like many former players have over the years … and see some of the guys and see some of the trainers and equipment staff and all the people I really care about that still work there. Yeah, I was definitely bummed out that we weren't in Lambeau for this one."

While Rodgers no longer plays for the Packers, his message for the team, the city, the organization, and the fans was clear.

Asked what he will miss the most when he is retired, Rodgers said: "Definitely the people I got to do it with." And that included Green Bay.

"That's what this game's all about," Rodgers added. "It's about the relationships, and I'm just most thankful for all the men and women, you know, who've been in my life through this game over the years. So many great people in Green Bay, in the entire organization, top to bottom. You know, just salt of the earth type of people. … But the thing that actually lasts the longest is those people that impact your life, and there's been a lot of those, a lot especially in Green Bay, it had a huge impact on my life. So I think about those people a lot."

title: Fact Check: FAKE Sports Journalist 'Marc Jacobs' Falsely Reported Russell Westbrook Was Signing With Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel
description: Did a real sports journalist named "Marc Jacobs" report that Russell Westbrook was signing with Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel? No, that's not true: There was no evidence that Westbrook, a 37-year-old NBA free agent, had signed with the Israeli...
fullText:
Did a real sports journalist named "Marc Jacobs" report that Russell Westbrook was signing with Hapoel Tel Aviv in Israel? No, that's not true: There was no evidence that Westbrook, a 37-year-old NBA free agent, had signed with the Israeli professional team as of Aug. 12, 2026. The claim came from a fake sports reporter on a parody account, citing a story that does not exist.

The claim appeared in a post and image (archived here) by the @MJacobsLF account on X on Aug. 9, 2026. It read:

REPORT: Russell #Westbrook and Hapoel Tel Aviv reportedly have mutual interest, with talks between the two sides continuing to expand. The former MVP is seriously considering a move overseas this season. Per @TheAthletic

A deal would mark the first time Westbrook plays professionally outside the NBA.

This is what the post looked like on X at the time of writing:

The Marc Jacobs X profile describes the persona as a "Senior NBA Writer & Reporter for @LakerFilm." Jacobs is not a mainstream, credentialed journalist and has fewer than 4,300 followers as of Aug. 12, 2026. The @LakerFilm account (archived here) had fewer than 40 followers as of Aug. 12, 2026, and had the display name "FOLLOW MJacobsLF."

Lead Stories searched Google News (archived here) and Yahoo News (archived here) and did not find any matching reports from credible news outlets reporting that Westbrook was in talks with Hapoel Tel Aviv. The searches used the terms "Russell Westbrook," "Hapoel Tel Aviv," and "Marc Jacobs."

However, several publications picked up the claim as legitimate reporting, including the Jerusalem Post (archived here), which later removed the story (archived here) from its website.

The post on X also falsely cited The Athletic (@TheAthletic) to substantiate its claim about Westbrook. The Athletic, owned by The New York Times Company, did not report the story (archived here). A Google Advanced Search of the site (archived here) by Lead Stories produced the same results.

Lead Stories ran the image of Westbrook in the post through Google Gemini (archived here), Google's AI assistant. The tool concluded that the image has a Google SynthID:
