title: Xavi becomes first non-Dutch Netherlands coach since 1978
description: Former Barcelona manager Xavi is appointed as the new head coach of the Netherlands on a four-year deal.
fullText:
Former Barcelona manager Xavi has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands on a four-year deal.

The 46-year-old, who played for Barcelona and Spain, will become the first non-Dutch coach to take charge of the Netherlands since Austrian coach Ernst Happel stepped down in 1978.

Ronald Koeman resigned as Netherlands manager following a last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer's World Cup.

"I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team," Xavi said.

"As someone who received his training at Barca's academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

"You could say that I am partly a son of Dutch football. Other great coaches, especially Louis van Gaal, under whom I made my debut at Barca, and Frank Rijkaard, also played an important role in shaping me as a player and coach."

Xavi will begin his Netherland's reign against Jurgen Klopp's Germany on 24 September in the Nations League.

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot confirmed he held talks over the job but withdrew because he wants his next role to be in club football.

Xavi, who won three international trophies, was part of the Spain team that beat the Netherlands in the 2010 World Cup final.

He retired in 2019 and went into management with Al-Sadd before taking over at Barca in November 2021, where he won a La Liga title in his first full season in charge.

It will be Xavi's first managerial job since he stepped down from Barcelona in 2024.

title: Everyone wants to 'tax the rich.' In New York City, it's getting complicated
description: Across the U.S., calls to “tax the rich” have become potent political slogans.  “It seems very simple but the more you dig into it, the more nuances you look at, the more complicated it gets,” said Ga...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Across the U.S., calls to "tax the rich" have become potent political slogans. But even in Mayor Zohran Mamdani's New York, getting the wealthy to pay more isn't playing out as smoothly as supporters hoped.

What seemed at first like an easy idea — slapping a new tax on people who own luxury second homes in the Big Apple but live elsewhere most of the year — has instead created a lot of confusion in the city's notoriously convoluted world of real estate arrangements.

"It seems very simple but the more you dig into it, the more nuances you look at, the more complicated it gets," said Gary Bingel, a state and local tax expert and partner at EisnerAmper, an accounting firm.

It has also prompted pushback from both the city's very wealthy and the merely moderately wealthy.

President Donald Trump, whose gilded Manhattan penthouse could be subject to the tax since his primary residence is now in Florida, said he was looking into whether federal intervention could "avert this disaster, before it is too late."

A group of homeowners sued over the city's rollout of the tax, arguing that officials had not done enough to figure out who would have to pay the tax and instead made it property owners' responsibility. A judge temporarily paused the process this week, but the city moved to appeal, allowing the tax effort to continue until it's sorted out in court.

Securing a new tax on multimillion-dollar second homes, known as pied-à-terres, was an early win for Mamdani in his quest to raise taxes on the city's highest earners to pay for his ambitious liberal agenda.

The so-called pied-à-terre tax would levy a new surcharge on one-, two- and three-family homes valued at more than $5 million, as well as condos and co-ops valued at $1 million or more, if those dwellings are not a person's primary residence.

The idea, according to officials, would bring $500 million to the city's coffers annually, paid primarily by bigwigs who get to enjoy city life but don't pay city income taxes.

That's where things start to get hairy.

It's common for high rollers to place their properties in trusts, obscuring ownership while allowing the property to pass more easily to family members. Limited liability companies can similarly shield an owner's identity, also making it hard for government officials to tell who actually lives in any given apartment.

From there, there are numerous arrangements that can complicate who would be subject to the tax. For example, letting a distant family member stay at a second home without formal documentation, or if someone owns one or more properties and rents them out, but the tenants don't have documentation that the unit is their primary residence.

"Those situations make it difficult to prove people are in there," said Mark Limardo, a partner at the law firm Herrick in Manhattan who focuses on taxes. "The concept is simple, but the ownership rules and the documentation rules have made it very complicated."

City Hall, for its part, argues that it shouldn't be difficult to provide proof that someone actually lives in the city and says that its finance department is experienced in parsing tangled webs of paperwork.

Mamdani, no stranger to razzing wealthy people, debuted the tax with a video singling out hedge fund CEO Ken Griffin by standing outside a Manhattan penthouse the billionaire purchased for around $239 million. The clip sent Mamdani's supporters swooning, but Griffin later said it was "frightening" that a public official would call attention to one of his homes, especially after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in the same neighborhood.

The city then published an expansive online list of property owners who it said could be subject to the tax, listing their names, addresses and property values. The list, which the city is legally required to publish, inflamed tensions between the mayor and the city's wealthy, many of whom argued the roll amounted to doxing or public shaming.

The administration has mailed notices to a much smaller group — about 17,000 properties — that it suspected would be subject to the tax, telling them they could apply for exemptions. Mamdani announced the mailers in a celebratory social media post that read: "If you have a second home in New York City worth more than $5M, check your mailbox when you're back in the five boroughs — because you've got mail."

He later pushed back the deadline for exemption requests following public outcry from people who claimed to have received the letters in error or had trouble navigating the process.

Stewart Sterk, a real estate law professor at Cardozo School of Law in New York, predicted last week's lawsuit wouldn't be the last, saying he expected many of the targets of the tax to file individual cases over denied exemptions, given the vast number of apartments at play and the various arrangements people have connecting them to their properties.

"This is going to be a subject of litigation for quite a while," he said.

title: Defense in Charlie Kirk's killing say shooter should not get death penalty, hit 'intended target'
description: The man charged with killing Charlie Kirk shouldn’t get the death penalty because the shooter “hit the intended target” and no one else was endangered when the conservative activist was shot from a ro...
fullText:
The man charged with killing Charlie Kirk shouldn't get the death penalty because the shooter "hit the intended target" and no one else was endangered when the conservative activist was shot from a rooftop at an event in Utah last year, his lawyers said.

Defendant Tyler Robinson's attorneys say the bullet traveled above the crowd of several thousand people at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10 and "there were no threats to others." Whether the shooting endangered the crowd is a key issue: Prosecutors cited the risk that other people could have been harmed as an aggravating factor under state law that makes Kirk's killing a capital crime.

"The only evidence presented supports that the bullet traveled above, not through, the crowd," defense attorneys wrote in documents filed late Tuesday as the defense tries to block the case from proceeding to trial.

Prosecutors have said numerous people were within a "zone of danger" around Kirk, where a stray or ricocheting bullet could have hurt anyone close to the victim.

The defense lawyers also disputed claims that Robinson targeted Kirk over his political views. Prosecutors allege Robinson told his roommate that he killed the activist because he "had enough of his hatred." But the defense said that was not enough to prove what motivated Robinson, after searches of his apartment, computers and telephone failed to produce anything beyond that one statement.

Prosecutors last month during a weeklong hearing presented what they call "overwhelming" evidence against Robinson, including DNA tests that tie him to the suspected murder weapon and apparent confessions by the defendant.

His attorneys questioned the reliability of the DNA tests and other evidence. They didn't offer any alternative theories for Kirk's assassination, and made no mention of DNA in Tuesday's filing.

Robinson is charged with aggravated murder and has not yet entered a plea. He turned himself in a day after Kirk was killed.

His defense attorneys previously tried to get the death penalty taken off the table after prosecutors were found to be in contempt of court for talking about the case to the media. State District Judge Tony Graf rejected that request.

In documents filed last month, prosecutors said the fact that Robinson loaded his rifle with four bullets showed that he knew he could miss Kirk, "thereby putting others in danger."

But defense attorneys said "it is just as likely that the shooter did not believe he would miss."

Robinson faces possible sentence enhancements if prosecutors can prove he targeted Kirk because of his politics. They contend that Kirk's strong opposition to same-sex marriage and gender transitioning stood in contrast to Robinson, who was in a romantic relationship with a roommate, Lance Twiggs. Twiggs told investigators that he had been considering transitioning around the time that Kirk was killed, according to prosecutors.

Twiggs also told investigators that Robinson sometimes talked about politics, including President Donald Trump. Yet Twiggs said he never heard Robinson talk about Kirk before the shooting. The defendant also did not talk much about gender issues or LGBTQ+ rights, Twiggs said. The AP emailed Twiggs' attorney seeking comment.

Closing arguments in the preliminary hearing are scheduled for Sept. 1. Graf will then decide if the case can go to trial and on what charges. Lawyers for Kirk's family have asked Graf to make his decision by or on Sept. 1 so the case can proceed.

Prosecutors have until Aug. 18 to respond to the latest defense arguments. The Associated Press left telephone and email messages with the Utah County Attorney's Office seeking comment.

Preliminary hearings typically don't last so long. Legal experts said the slow pace reflects a cautious approach by Graf, the large volume of evidence and a desire by prosecutors to disprove conspiracy theories around the case.

title: Rybakina comeback knocks Osaka out of Canadian Open
description: Elena Rybakina comes back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina came back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final.

Four-time Grand Slam winner Osaka had won the first set and was 4-2 up in the second before her Kazakh rival came back to win 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 in two hours and 33 minutes.

"I was just trying to fight," said Rybakina, whose 72 unforced errors were her most in a match this season.

"The first game was really tough because it cost me the set, and then in the second I was just trying to stay closer to the score, even if I'm losing. I'm super happy that I won this match."

Japan's Osaka broke Rybakina in the opening game on the way to claiming the first set in Toronto.

The second set appeared to be going Osaka's way as, despite having one break retrieved, she broke again to go 4-2 up against the the 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open champion.

However, Rybakina took three straight games and won the tie-break to level the match.

Osaka had four break points when she led 3-2 in the decider but failed to take them as Rybakina held and then broke her opponent in the next game.

Rybakina went on to emphatically serve out for the match, sealing victory with a 15th ace and she will play Coco Gauff in the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, Osaka said she was withdrawing from the Cincinnati Open, the last tournament before the US Open, because of "fatigue".

Gauff progressed after Belinda Bencic withdrew from their match with a hip injury.

The other semi-final will be between Iga Swiatek, a 6-2 6-1 winner against Diana Shnaider, and Elina Svitolina, who beat Ekaterina Alexandrova 3-6 6-0 6-3.

title: Lukaku seals 'emotional' move to Fenerbahce
description: Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku has joined Turkish side Fenerbahce from Napoli for an undisclosed fee and contract length.
fullText:
Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku has joined Turkish side Fenerbahce from Napoli.

The 33-year-old struggled with injuries last season and made only seven appearances in all competitions for the Serie A side.

Belgium's record goalscorer returns to Turkey where he lived during the 1996-1997 season when his father Roger was playing professionally for the Super Lig club Genclerbirligi.

"It's an honour and a privilege to be joining your club ," said Lukaku in a video on social media addressed to Fenerbahce's fans.

"I am fit, 100%, ready to go. It is an emotional moment after many years to be going back to Turkey where I lived as a young kid, where I discovered the professional world as a toddler with my dad."

The fee and length of contract for Lukaku has not been disclosed.

Despite an injury-hit campaign last season, the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scored three goals at this summer's World Cup.

Lukaku has won the Belgian championship with Anderlecht, a Fifa Club World Cup with Chelsea, and a Scudetto with both Inter Milan and Napoli.

He is the second former United forward to join the club this summer after Mason Greenwood was signed from Marseille.

Fenerbahce, who have finished runners-up to Galatasaray for the last four seasons, are without a Turkish league title since 2014.

As of Wednesday, Ocasio-Cortez had an 18 percent chance of winning the Democratic nomination on Polymarket, narrowly ahead of Newsom at 17 percent.

Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) ranked third at about 16 percent, according to the data.

The New York Democrat has drawn increased attention this week after announcing she's freezing her eggs. She has also been documenting the process on her social media, which received mixed reactions.

Despite Ocasio-Cortez's lead on Polymarket, traders on Kalshi still rank Newsom as the favorite.

title: Solar eclipse distracts from sporting events - in pictures
description: Pictures from sporting events as the most significant solar eclipse since 1999 is visible across the UK and Europe on Wednesday.
fullText:
The most significant solar eclipse since 1999 was visible across the UK and Europe on Wednesday and briefly took attention away from various sporting events in the process.

A total solar eclipse peaked in parts of Spain and Iceland.

In the UK, people could see a partial eclipse with more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon depending one where you were.

Whether you were at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham, a Hundred cricket match or Aston Villa's Super Cup game against Paris St-Germain in Austria, sports fans paused to take in the rare sight.

Experts told watchers not to look directly at the Sun without protection, which saw many supporters who did not have glasses come up with home-made solutions.

title: Jaissle 'aware' of Newcastle needs after Everton friendly loss
description: Matthias Jaissle says he is "aware" of Newcastle's shortcomings after a comfortable 3-1 friendly defeat by Everton.
fullText:
The stadium announcer at the home of Scottish rugby was certainly excited.

"Expect passion and world-class football from the very first whistle," he roared before Newcastle United met Everton in a pre-season friendly at Murrayfield.

However, pre-season, or not, this was always going to be a useful exercise for new Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle, as he came up against top-flight opposition just a week and a half before the new campaign starts.

The 3-1 defeat certainly served as a reminder of the work that is still required, not only on the training pitches but in the transfer market, too.

"You all see the matches," he said. "You are also smart enough to see the needs in the squad.

"I will be always consistent with my approach. We handle these things internally. We are aware of what we need. Let's see now. There is still some time."

There was a fresh look to this Newcastle side in the opening stages and fearless new signing Bazoumana Toure again caught the eye with his pace down the left.

However, Jaissle's team were unable to capitalise on a bright start - spurning a number of opportunities in front of goal - and they looked increasingly vulnerable at the back as the first half wore on.

A simple long ball forward from James Tarkowski caused havoc in the build-up to Everton's opener in the 27th minute after Thierno Barry nipped in ahead of shaky Newcastle centre-back Sven Botman to race clear.

Although Lewis Hall got back to make a recovery tackle, he could only hook the ball away as far as Harrison Armstrong, who coolly picked out Barry to finish past goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek from inside the box.

Jaissle punched the palm of his hand in frustration on the touchline before gesturing to his players to go again, just as they did when they came from behind to beat Valencia 2-1 in his first friendly at the weekend.

But Iliman Ndiaye doubled Everton's lead from the penalty spot a few minutes later after Joelinton was rather harshly adjudged to have fouled Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall inside the box.

That was the cue for taunts of "going down, going down, going down" from Everton supporters.

Once Tyrique George made it 3-0, with a drilled effort in the 73rd minute, a number of Newcastle fans started to make their way for the exit - and not to catch a glimpse of the solar eclipse.

However, there was still time for substitute Harvey Barnes to pull one back after he slammed the ball home at the back post from Jacob Murphy's cross.

Barnes and Murphy also featured when Newcastle tasted defeat against Everton in the Premier League under former head coach Eddie Howe back in February.

But this was a drastically different starting line-up following a summer of change on Tyneside.

Eight of the starters were aged 25 and under while Joelinton, who wore the captain's armband, and Yoane Wissa were the oldest by a considerable distance at 29.

Newcastle still have important figures like Dan Burn, Lewis Miley and Tino Livramento to return - albeit the trio are unlikely to all feature in the season opener versus Liverpool - but this squad clearly needs further reinforcements in the transfer market.

That won't come as news to sporting director Ross Wilson, who was among those watching on at Murrayfield on Wednesday night, or Jaissle.

It was rather telling that the German again referenced a "vacuum" for the second time in two days following the departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Kieran Trippier earlier this summer.

"You cannot change things really quickly," he said. "It's a really young team at the moment so there are vacuums where players need to step up.

"We fill these positions we lost with the experienced players, but that's also the process."

Newcastle remain in the market for a right-back, an older central midfielder and, depending on Jaissle's assessment of the squad, potentially another addition beyond that before the window shuts on 1 September.

There are still a couple of friendlies to play before Liverpool visit St James' Park next week, but there is little time to waste.

"If you make new signings at the end of the transfer window, they usually need time," Jaissle added. "Usually it takes time to adapt to the Premier League.

"Those are all things we consider, but we are all still positive. We all want to go in the right direction.

"We have these goals and there's many stones along the way thrown in that path, but we need to get rid of them."

title: Law firm with ties to Trump administration declines offer to represent migrant children
description: A small Texas law firm with ties to the Trump administration declined a $150 million federal contract it was offered to represent migrant children traveling alone to the U.S., authorities said Wednesd...
fullText:
McALLEN, Texas (AP) — A small Texas law firm with ties to the Trump administration declined a $150 million federal contract it was offered to represent migrant children traveling alone to the U.S., authorities said Wednesday, raising long-term questions about who would represent them.

The administration last week announced plans to award the contract to the Burke Law Group, a Houston-based firm with little experience in immigration. The contract offer came as the administration ramps up its mass deportation campaign and after it let a key contract with nearly 100 providers working with immigrant children around the country expire at the end of July with no replacement.

Unaccompanied migrant children in federal custody are being temporarily represented by another group, but it is unclear how things will shake out after its contract expires in December. A Wednesday statement from the federal Office of Refugee Resettlement, which oversees the contracts, offered no insight into why Burke declined the offer.

"Burke Law Group has declined to apply and has not been awarded any grant," the agency, which is part of the Department of Health and Human Services, said in an emailed statement in response to a query about the contract.

Burke Law Group published a short statement on social media Tuesday night saying it had considered applying for a "small portion" of the contract. It did not explain why it decided against it.

Burke Law Group's founder, Marcella Burke, served in President Donald Trump's first administration as a lawyer with the Environmental Protection Agency and the Department of the Interior.

Others on its roster include Justin Shubow, a supporter of Trump's efforts to require federal buildings to adhere to classical and traditional architectural styles, and a former Trump appointee to the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts. Prominent conservative legal scholar Ilya Shapiro is listed as senior counsel.

Migrant children who are detained after entering the U.S. without their parents are usually entrusted to federal government care. Congress created various legal protections for them, including the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008, which requires the government to provide legal representation for children put into deportation proceedings.

About 1,800 children were living in shelters and roughly 22,000 facing deportation were living with outside sponsors such as family members, according to the legal service providers whose contract expired.

The Burke Law Group, with fewer than 30 lawyers and only two with relevant immigration experience listed on its website, was one of two groups tapped by the government to fill in the gap.

A temporary contract for $20 million was awarded through the end of the year to the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants, a legal aid group whose previous work with the government involved helping resettle Afrikaners.

Attorneys with USCRI started showing up in immigration court last week, unannounced, claiming to represent children they had not yet met and sparking confusion among judges and lawyers from the expired contract still providing representation.

Some legal aid providers whose contracts expired sued the administration after they went without payment since last year. On Aug. 6, a California federal judge ordered the federal government to pay the providers.

"These half-baked plans are not sufficient to comply with this court's order," Caelin Moriarity Miltko, an attorney representing the providers, told the judge last week, referring to the interim contracts the government is trying to set up.

"Plaintiffs have ethical obligations to the children they represent today, to continue providing that representation to the best of their abilities, and that representation cannot transfer instantaneously to a new group simply because defendants have changed the contract," Miltko said.

Bilal Askaryar, director of communications at Acacia Center for Justice, the organization that handled the expired contract with the government, confirmed on Wednesday that the groups started to receive payments covering six out of nine months owed, with the rest in progress.

title: Guimaraes makes Arsenal debut in draw with Como
description: Bruno Guimaraes put in an assured performance as he made his Arsenal debut in a 1-1 friendly draw with Como at Emirates stadium.
fullText:
Bruno Guimaraes put in an assured performance as he made his Arsenal debut in a 1-1 friendly draw with Como at Emirates stadium.

The £75m signing from Newcastle United was officially announced on Saturday, then introduced to the club's supporters before their friendly with Dortmund on Sunday.

Fans arrived at Emirates on Wednesday evening in anticipation of seeing the Brazilian international in action, but had to wait until half-time.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, whose future has been much debated in the past couple of days following reported interest from rivals Chelsea and Manchester United, opened the scoring in the first half.

But the Gunners were then pegged back by an excellent strike from Martin Baturina before Guimaraes was introduced.

Chants of "Bruno" rang out around the ground as the new number 39 stepped on to the pitch, followed by cheers as he had his first touch of the ball.

Guimaraes - known for his combative, all-action style - put in a recovery tackle to stop a Como counter-attack before passing the ball to David Raya, with the passage of play cheered like a goal.

There were early signs of a partnership between Guimaraes and Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard, too.

Mikel Arteta had named an experimental side for this game, with five academy graduates in the starting XI.

But as the game hit the hour mark, Arteta brought on what could be considered his strongest available side, with thoughts of the Community Shield against Manchester City on Sunday.

Guimaraes had been playing alongside Lewis-Skelly but once he was withdrawn, as Mikel Merino and Odegaard were introduced from the substitutes bench, the new signing dropped to be the deepest-lying player in the Arsenal midfield.

The match drifted as the changes and a second-half drinks break affected the flow of the game, but Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke and Cristhian Mosquera all had efforts before the end of the match.

Guimaraes tried a chipped pass behind the Como defence, which Havertz finished, but the offside flag was up to rule the strike out.

The pass over the defence is something the midfielder tried a couple of times and will give supporters encouragement he can help the Gunners find their attacking flow as the season gets under way.

This is not a performance that will define Guimaraes' time in north London, but the fact he settled in so seamlessly is exactly why Arsenal bought him for the large fee.

After the match followed a pre-agreed penalty shootout and Guimaraes boldly scored his spot-kick, which will give him a confidence boost before the first competitive match of Arsenal's season on Sunday.

Arteta was asked in his post-match news conference if the midfielder would be ready to start against Manchester City.

"Let's see. He only had three training sessions. But he looked good," he said,

"He was really pushing to play some minutes today. I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"You sensed immediately a really strong connection and a player that is going to make us better without a doubt."

What's happening with Lewis-Skelly's Arsenal future?

Arsenal reignite interest in Aston Villa's Konsa

There was a lot of noise around Lewis-Skelly coming into this match.

The 19-year-old has been linked with a move away from the Gunners in the past couple of days, with Manchester United and Chelsea two of the sides reported to have been offered the midfielder - something Arsenal denies.

Lewis-Skelly made a heart gesture towards all sides of the crowd after he opened the scoring against Como, in a seemingly pointed celebration.

"He's a very emotional player," Arteta said when asked about Lewis-Skelly's goal.

"Remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch?"

"I am not going to talk about any speculation. If there is any speculation about our players it is a good sign, it means we attract attention and they are doing a good job," Arteta added.

The Gunners boss was then asked about the bond between supporters and players who come through the club's academy.

"Well its a natural thing to happen - we have seen it with many other players here," Arteta said.

title: Chelsea set Friday deadline over £120m Fernandez
description: Chelsea set a Friday deadline for offers of £120m for clubs interested in midfielder Enzo Fernandez.
fullText:
Chelsea have set a Friday deadline for offers of £120m or more from clubs interested in midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

The Argentina international, 25, has faced uncertainty over his future at Stamford Bridge since March, when he first raised the possibility of a move to Real Madrid.

Around that time, his agent Javier Pastore publicly stated his client was underpaid and wanted to leave following a difficult season in which Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League and ended the campaign without a trophy after losing the FA Cup final to Manchester City.

The late-bloomer left-back joining Chelsea for £16m

Real Madrid have since said they have "no intention" of signing Fernandez, leaving the only known potential suitors as Manchester City, whose new boss Enzo Maresca left Chelsea midway through last season.

It remains unclear whether City would be willing to meet the player's valuation, with the Etihad outfit also known to be targeting Lille's Moroccan midfielder Ayoub Bouaddi.

Chelsea have set a deadline of 17:00 BST on Friday for any offers and are expected to stand firm on their £120m price tag, even though they signed him for £107m from Benfica in 2023.

The deadline is intended to bring an end to uncertainty before the start of the season, having given Fernandez and any interested clubs around 60 days to complete a deal at what Chelsea consider a fair price.

New manager Xabi Alonso has spoken to Fernandez about his future, but has declined to disclose details of their conversation.

It is understood Chelsea have made it clear they are willing to fully reintegrate Fernandez into the squad and allow him to continue as a key player.

He scored 15 goals and provided seven assists in 54 appearances for the club last season. He then helped Argentina reach the World Cup final, where he was sent off as they lost to Spain 1-0.

Fernandez returned to training with Chelsea this week for the first time under Alonso.

title: GB's Evans wins European gold in 100m breaststroke
description: Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.
fullText:
Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 23-year-old comfortably finished first in a championship record time of one minute and 4.87 seconds, which was also a lifetime best and British record.

Having also broken the championship record in the semi-final, Evans claimed gold ahead of Ireland's Mona McSharry in second, while Italy's Benedetta Pilato took bronze.

Great Britain's Filip Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games last month in Glasgow, was the fastest qualifier in the semi-final of the same event at the European Aquatics Championships.

The 18-year-old's time of 2:08.60 held off GB team-mate Greg Butler in the first semi-final, with the 25-year-old also progressing to the final.

GB's Amalie Smith picked up a silver medal in the 400m individual medley final, finishing 0.7secs behind Ireland's Ellen Walshe, with Poland's Justina Kozan claiming bronze.

The 16-year-old Smith, who won gold on Monday in the 4x200m freestyle relay, was also part of the part of the 4x100m freestyle relay team that finished fifth.

Another teenager, Italian Sara Curtis, also shone as she broke the women's 50m backstroke world record with a time of 26.63 seconds.

The 19-year-old bettered the world record set by Australia's Kaylee McKeown three years ago by 0.23secs in her semi-final.

title: Florida deputy killed ex-girlfriend over a TV, then himself, sheriff says
description: Deputy Troy Savetz waited outside his ex-girlfriend's home with a gun, angry over a TV set, before abducting her as her children called 911 from inside.
fullText:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

A Florida sheriff's deputy, honored multiple times for his bravery, dedication and compassion, killed a former girlfriend and then himself Monday after an argument over a television.

The victim was identified by friends as Mandy Fackler, who leaves behind two children, 12 and 9, Fox Tampa reported.

Deputy Troy Savetz had been with the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office for 14 years and was a member of the marine unit.

He and the victim had an "on-again-off-again, tumultuous relationship," Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri said in a news conference.

Missouri Mom Of 5 Fatally Shot While Buying Slushies With Children; Police Search For Gunman

Savetz, 47, was waiting outside Fackler's home when she and her children returned from a day at the beach at about 5:30 p.m. He brandished a gun and was angry about "wanting his TV set back," Gualtieri said.

When the victim tried to call 911, Savetz took her phone. That's when she told her two children to go inside.

They did as they were told. And they never saw her again.

The children were "extremely brave," calling 911 and giving dispatchers everything needed to identify the suspect, Pasco County Sheriff Chris Nocco told reporters.

When authorities arrived at the home, they saw the mother's vehicle with the door wide open, and they found her phone, Nocco said.

"At that point, they realize that she's no longer there" at the residence, he said.

Officers sprang into action using K-9 teams, drones and aviation units, searching for the vehicle Savetz was driving when he carried the victim away, Nocco said.

About 90 minutes after the altercation began, authorities found the vehicle in nearby Spring Hill. Officers approached with a drone and saw two people inside.

When they reached the car on foot, they found Savetz and his victim dead.

"We're not sure when and at what point" he killed her and himself, Nocco said.

The children, now with their biological father, were unharmed in the incident.

Dispatch Audio Released In Michigan Family Murder-suicide As Troubled Family's Secrets Emerge

They "should be starting off this week getting ready for school," Nocco said. Instead, they're "starting off this week getting ready for a sad life without their mother."

He praised the children for their bravery and obedience at such a critical moment.

"I know eventually there's going to be a point in your life where you're going to go back and listen to all the videos and read all the reports," Nocco said.

"So please hear this directly from us: We listened to that 911 tape, and we know that your mother said to go inside to save your lives and to call 911. You did exactly what your mom asked you to do.

"Know this: Your mom is looking down from heaven, and she's so proud of you two … So know that you two did the right thing."

Nocco said officers were "amazed" by the children's "calmness." The information they provided allowed for the fastest possible response.

"So we're so proud of you, and I know your mom is. But know [that] this entire community is praying for you."

Off-duty Trooper And Armed Citizen Hailed As Heroes After Returning Fire On In-n-out Gunman

Before this, Savetz had earned accolades for his behavior while wearing the badge. In 2014, he was honored by the sheriff's office for his "heroic action" in saving the life of a 24-year-old man, stopping him from jumping off a bridge in Pinellas County.

That earned him attention from the Tampa Bay Rays baseball team, who called him "Our Everyday MVP" in a June 2015 social media post. Wearing his green uniform, Savetz was honored by receiving the opportunity to throw out a ceremonial first pitch.

He was hailed a "hero" at local fundraisers and by radio stations.

In 2018, the sheriff's office shared a social media post about how Savetz had adopted a pot-bellied pig he found while on duty. That year, he and Maple, as she became known, went on to be named ambassadors for the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals in Tampa Bay.

But the "inexcusable" behavior of Savetz immediately ended his identity as a law enforcement officer, Gualtieri said.

"The moment this individual committed a crime, he was no longer a law enforcement officer. He was a criminal."

title: Messi's most iconic moments as he ponders retirement
description: As Lionel Messi considers his footballing future following the death of his father, BBC Sport looks back at some of his most iconic moments.
fullText:
Lionel Messi is considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge.

The 39-year-old Argentina forward is signed with Inter Miami until 2028.

But, in an emotional tribute to his dad, he hinted at retirement as he said: "I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer."

He has scored a combined 921 goals for Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Inter Miami and Argentina.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of his remarkable career.

Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death

A rivalry that changed football

'That's why he's the king' - Messi sets up third World Cup final

Messi's first career hat-trick came in one of the biggest fixtures in football - El Clasico.

At the age of 19, he scored all of Barcelona's goals in a 3-3 draw against rivals Real Madrid on 10 March 2007 - his first at the Camp Nou - including a brilliant last-minute finish after beating a couple of defenders.

This was arguably the moment he became a household name.

Just over a month after that hat-trick, Messi scored a goal he has probably never surpassed in the rest of his glorious career.

It came in a 5-2 win over Getafe in the Copa del Rey semi-final first leg on 18 April 2007.

In a strike with remarkable similarities to compatriot Diego Maradona's (non-handball) effort against England in the 1986 World Cup, Messi picked the ball up in his own half, beat about five defenders, went around the goalkeeper and slotted home.

Ridiculous as it sounds now, back in 2009 some English football fans and journalists questioned whether Messi could do it against English opponents in Europe - having failed to net in 10 Champions League appearances against Premier League sides.

But there were no more doubts when Messi rose highest in the box to head home Xavi's cross in his first Champions League final against Manchester United - and the first game billed as Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo.

Two years later he would score in another final win over Sir Alex Ferguson's men to claim the third of his four Champions League winners' medals.

Messi scored four goals for the first time in his career as he took Arsenal to the cleaners in the 2010 Champions League quarter-final for a 4-1 home-leg win.

The pick of the bunch was his chip over keeper Manuel Almunia to complete his hat-trick.

An honourable mention goes to his five-goal haul two years later against Bayer Leverkusen in a 7-1 last-16 success.

He is the second top scorer in Champions League history with 129, behind Ronaldo.

Messi broke Barcelona's goalscoring record - aged just 24 - in some style with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Granada on 20 March 2012.

He equalled Cesar Rodriguez's 60-year-old record of 232 goals with his first, broke it with his second and extended the record with a third.

A stat so amazing you have to go back to double check to make sure it really happened.

In 2012 Messi hit his 91st goal of the year in Barcelona's 3-1 win at Real Valladolid on 22 December.

It earned him a place in the Guinness Book of Records., external

He netted 79 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina - in a total of 69 games for club and country.

It was enough to earn Messi a then-unprecedented fourth consecutive Ballon d'Or - even though he only won the Copa del Rey in 2012 for all those goals.

This was the second major record Messi broke with a hat-trick.

He hit three in a 5-1 win over Sevilla on 22 November 2014 to become the top scorer in La Liga's history.

Messi equalled Telmo Zarra's 251-goal mark - set in 1955 by the Athletic Club forward - with a free-kick, before breaking it and stretching it with a third.

He ended up on 474 goals, far clear of Ronaldo's 311 for Real Madrid.

All the narratives seemed to come together in Barcelona's 3-2 win at Real Madrid on 23 April 2017.

Messi popped up with an injury-time goal, sweeping home a first-time shot from the edge of the area. It was an El Clasico winner, his 500th Barcelona goal and it sent his side top of the table - although Real would go on to win the league at the end of that season.

For good measure, he pulled out an iconic celebration when he took off his shirt and held it out so the Bernabeu faithful could see his name.

The almost unthinkable happened in August 2021 as Messi left Barcelona on a free transfer.

After 21 years, 672 goals and 35 trophies, he had to leave because the club could not afford to honour the new contract they agreed because of La Liga's salary limit.

In an emotional news conference, a tearful Messi said: "My family and I were convinced we were going to stay here, at home.

"I don't want to leave this club - it's a club I love and this is a moment I didn't expect."

Despite being linked with Manchester City, he joined Paris St-Germain.

On 11 July, 2021, Messi - at the age of 34 - won his first senior international trophy as Argentina beat Brazil 1-0 in the Copa America final at the Maracana.

He was named player of the tournament after scoring four goals.

An emotional Messi fell to the ground as the full-time whistle blew and was thrown in the air by his team-mates as they celebrated.

He won his second Copa America three years later.

It was a triumph and moment that looked like it would never happen, with Messi having previously retired from international football before coming back.

It was always the thing held against him in debates about whether he was the greatest footballer of all time.

Messi scored two goals, and his effort in the 2022 shootout, as Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the best World Cup final ever.

He was named player of the tournament, having netted seven times - including efforts in each knockout round.

Messi won another two Ballons d'Or after leaving Barcelona - one at Paris St-Germain and one at Inter Miami - to extend his record haul to eight.

His last one came in October 2023 after he won the World Cup and helped his Major League Soccer side lift the Leagues Cup for their first trophy.

"I couldn't imagine having the career I've had and everything I've achieved, the fortune I've had to be part of the best team in history," he said.

"All of them [Ballon d'Or awards] are special for different reasons."

If 2026 was to be his last World Cup, Messi certainly went out in style.

His eight goals in the tournament took him 21 in the World Cup - more than anyone has ever scored, until Mbappe went past that tally to 22 in the Bronze Final defeat by England.

Aged 39, Messi's World Cup may have ended in disappointment - as Argentina lost to Spain in the final - but individually it was another month on football's biggest stage few will forget.

title: Fernandes the centre of attention - but what next for Man Utd captain?
description: Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes is attracting attention on and off the pitch.
fullText:
Bruno Fernandes was the centre of attention in every sense on a historic night at Croke Park.

One of the biggest cheers of the evening from a sell-out crowd for the first 'soccer' match between English teams at the 82,500-capacity home of the Gaelic Athletic Association came after an hour of Manchester United's pre-season game with Leeds, when Fernandes' name was read out as one of five substitutes being made by head coach Michael Carrick.

The place would have erupted if either Fernandes had not had an effort ruled out for offside, or his shot from the edge of the area had gone in, not flicked off the bar.

The hero worship was taken too far when first one fan, then another, then another raced on to the pitch to get a selfie. With chaos threatening to take hold and 90 minutes played, the match was called to a halt without injury time, and went straight to penalties.

Amazingly, Fernandes missed, although Noussair Mazraoui kept his cool a few minutes later to secure a 5-4 victory, after the game itself had been brought to a premature conclusion at 1-1.

The result was irrelevant compared to preparations for the new season.

But the reaction for Fernandes underlines his hero status among United fans, which was established long before his nine goals and record 21 assists ensured a third-place finish in the Premier League last season and secured a return to the Champions League.

Of all United's squad, Fernandes is the one worshipped by fans.

But after the 'will-he, won't-he' debate around the 31-year-old's future last summer when the massive offer from Saudi Pro-League side Al-Hilal emerged, United's resolve could be about to be tested again.

Italian heavyweights Juventus and AC Milan, plus Galatasaray, are all understood to be keen on the Portugal playmaker, who has a £57m release clause available to overseas clubs.

It remains to be seen how United react if a bid is received. Last December, Fernandes admitted to being "hurt" at being told by United officials it was up to him whether he wanted to accept the Al-Hilal offer.

Now, his contract has entered its final year - there is an option to extend by a further season - and, as yet, there is no agreement over a new one.

It is thought Fernandes' preference is to stay at United, potentially for the remainder of his career. On the club's previous visit to the Republic of Ireland in April, he said he wants to compete for trophies. That situation is understood still to be the case.

But at a time when United are attempting to keep a lid on their wage bill, Fernandes could justifiably point to his contribution as being worthy of a significant salary, as Marcus Rashford returns to the club and is currently the highest earner.

United's hierarchy may find themselves with a problem that won't easily be resolved.

Certainly, Carrick won't want to lose the former Sporting man.

Already, Fernandes' partnership with new arrival Youri Tielemans is starting to pay dividends.

It was Tielemans who set his captain up for the shot that struck the bar, the short pass evidence of the understanding developing between the pair, which the Belgium midfielder outlined speaking to the media on Tuesday.

Marcus Rashford, along with England team-mate Kobbie Mainoo and Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez, were not involved in the game.

Rashford and Mainoo returned to training on Monday after their World Cup stints, with Martinez arriving in Dublin a day later after reaching the final.

They could come into contention for Saturday's final pre-season game against AC Milan in Wroclaw.

For Rashford, it would mean an encounter with Ruben Amorim, who he fell out with within weeks of his arrival from Sporting in November 2024. Amorim famously did not pick Mainoo to start a Premier League game before he was sacked in January.

It had not been anticipated Rashford would return to United when he joined Barcelona on loan just over 12 months ago.

However, Barca opted not to pay the £26m needed to make the transfer permanent and now it looks increasingly likely Rashford will remain with United and play under Carrick, a former team-mate, coach and, for three games following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's dismissal in November 2021, temporary boss.

"He's our player," Carrick told ITV. "He's come back great.

"I've known him a long time and he gives us something a little bit different."

title: Atletico agree £34.2m deal for Tottenham's Romero
description: Cristian Romero is set to join La Liga side Atletico Madrid as they agree a £34.2m fee with Tottenham for their captain.
fullText:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a £34.2m (40m euros) fee to sign Cristian Romero from Tottenham.

The 28-year-old is set to become Atletico's fourth signing of the summer, while Spurs will also retain a 15 per cent sell-on clause as part of the deal.

Argentina international Romero was the subject of interest from Premier League champions Arsenal in recent days, but Tottenham did not want to sell their captain to their north London rivals.

He leaves Tottenham after five seasons, having made 156 appearances for them, scoring 13 times, following an initial campaign on loan from Atalanta in 2021.

The centre-back played for Argentina during their run to the World Cup final this summer, missing just one game.

Romero was scheduled to return to pre-season with Spurs in the coming week after being given extra time off following the tournament in North America.

He captained the side last season as Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation from the Premier League.

Having signed permanently from Atalanta in a £42.5m deal, Romero became a key figure in their defence.

The news will be a blow to Spurs fans who are also set to lose Djed Spence to Inter Milan, who are in advanced talks to sign the England full-back in a £25.6m (30m euros) deal.

With the additions of midfielders Kang-in Lee and Morten Hjulmand and left-back Alejandro Grimaldo, Atletico are set to take their transfer spending over £100m this summer should they complete the Romero deal.

Head coach Diego Simeone is aiming to strengthen his squad after they finished fourth in La Liga last season, with Villarreal beating them to third place.

title: GB's Hudson-Smith wins historic 400m gold on home track - highlights & report
description: Great Britain's Matthew Hudson-Smith makes history as the joint-most decorated man of all-time at European Championships by claiming 400m gold in Birmingham.
fullText:
On his childhood track, in front of a stand named in his honour, hometown hero Matthew Hudson-Smith was not going to be denied.

A full-circle moment, completed by writing his name in history.

More than two decades after stepping foot inside Alexander Stadium for the first time aged nine, Hudson-Smith delivered Great Britain's latest gold in Birmingham to become the joint-most decorated man of all-time at European Championships.

The 31-year-old celebrated the third European 400m title of his illustrious career by making his way into the crowd and placing a hand on the banner bearing his name.

Moments before, Hudson-Smith had stormed down the home straight, just as he had countless times before as a member of local club Birchfield Harriers.

This time, though, the Olympic and world silver medallist did so to rapturous cheers inside the arena which fostered his love for the sport.

With his eighth podium at the championships, Hudson-Smith equalled French sprinter Christophe Lemaitre's men's record medal tally - with the relays still to come.

"Honestly, words can't describe how much that meant to me," he told BBC Sport.

"Nobody was going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I know this track like the back of my hand. I have my stand. Now I'm going to go for Mayor of Birmingham and Wolverhampton!

"I knew I was the best in the world. I knew that, on paper, I was a second faster than every single one of these guys. It was about me and the clock."

The team behind Hodgkinson's golden rise and the hunt for a world record

European Athletics Championships medal table

It is 12 years since Hudson-Smith won the first of his European Championship medals, claiming 400m silver on his debut in 2014.

Since then he has dealt only in golds in his individual event at this level, alongside two 4x400m relay titles.

With this latest triumph, Hudson-Smith joined British greats Mo Farah and Roger Black on five gold medals, while matching Dina Asher-Smith as the most decorated British athlete in the history of the championships.

It was Great Britain's third gold of the championships, while Emily Newnham added the hosts' sixth medal overall with silver in the women's 400m hurdles final shortly after Hudson-Smith's victory.

The hosts have further gold medal hopes on Thursday, after newly crowned 100m champion Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith both qualified for the women's 200m final by winning their heats, while Max Burgin and Ben Pattison will contest the men's 800m final, and Elise Thorner will bid for steeplechase glory.

Born in Wolverhampton, Hudson-Smith said before the championships that it would "mean the world" to land gold not only home soil, but where he first began working towards his dreams.

With his achievements since those early training sessions recognised in writing on the north stand, to Hudson-Smith's mind there could be only one possible outcome.

He did not make it easy for himself, however.

Entering the championships as the fastest European this year, the Briton admitted he "misjudged" his semi-final after fading to second place in his heat - an error which meant he had to pursue gold from the outside lane.

Unable to monitor the early progress of his rivals, Hudson-Smith went out hard and had established enough of a gap entering the home straight to reassure the home fans that all was under control.

The European record holder over 400m, and the sixth-fastest man of all time in the one-lap event, missed out on successive global titles by mere fractions of a second at both the World Championships in 2023 and Paris 2024 Olympics.

Those stunning silvers followed the toughest period of his life, but he put three years of "absolute hell" behind him to win world bronze in 2022 as he re-established himself among the world's best.

On the European stage, there has been no shortage of golden moments - but none will come close to this emotional full-circle moment.

Gold was secured in 44.17 seconds, with Frenchman Muhammad Abdallah Kounta next to cross the line in 44.40.

Speaking on BBC TV, three-time world heptathlon champion Dame Jessica Ennis-Hill said: "What a moment. This will stay with Matthew Hudson-Smith forever.

"It means so much and the pressure was piled on him. Anything but a gold medal here for him would have been a disappointment."

Hudson-Smith's celebrations had not long concluded when the 22-year-old Newnham achieved her latest international medal of a sensational season.

Delivering from lane nine, just as Hudson-Smith had done just 20 minutes earlier, she produced a personal best of 53.33 seconds to take silver behind Slovakia's Emma Zapletalova, who won in 52.91.

In a breakthrough 2025, Newnham won two relay medals as part of the British team at the European Indoor Championships, and double gold - including individual success - at the European Under-23 Championships.

Building on that progress, she lowered both her 400m hurdles and 400m flat personal bests this summer before clinching her first individual senior international medal at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow 12 days ago.

This latest glimpse of her exciting potential took her closer still to 1992 Olympic champion Sally Gunnell's British record of 52.74, which has stood for 33 years.

title: 4-year-old dies after suffering electrical shock from clothes dryer inside Kansas home
description: Authorities say the 4-year-old suffered an apparent electrical shock from a 220v clothes dryer while playing inside a southeastern Kansas home.
fullText:
A 4-year-old child died in a "tragic accident" last Thursday after being electrocuted by a clothes dryer, according to Kansas officials.

The incident happened in Savonburg, Kansas, while the child was "playing" inside a home, the Allen County Sheriff's Office (ACSO) said in a statement Saturday.

The child "allegedly received an electrical shock from a 220v dryer," the sheriff's office said.

The parents rushed their child, who was reportedly unconscious, to a local hospital around 9:30 p.m., according to authorities.

Georgia Teacher, Father Hailed As Hero After Dying To Save Girl From Myrtle Beach Rip Current

However, the child was later pronounced dead at the hospital.

No foul play is suspected at this time, and the ACSO is investigating the incident.

Officials extended their condolences to the family and responders involved following the incident.

"The Sheriff's Office extends our heartfelt condolences to the family members and all those affected by this tragedy, including the Allen County dispatchers, first responders, and hospital personnel," the office said.

A 220-volt electrical current, which was involved in Thursday's accident, can cause serious injury or death, including cardiac arrest.

Man, Woman Killed In Rip Current As Lifeguard Shortage Leaves Danger Zones In Beach Destination

While clothes dryers have been linked to thousands of home fires annually, primarily caused by lint buildup blocking exhaust ducts or overheating electrical elements, electrical deaths involving major laundry appliances are considered extremely rare.

In one of the rare instances, a 10-year-old boy was found dead inside a dryer at a Houston-area apartment complex in 2018, according to Fox 5 DC.

A medical examiner determined the boy had been electrocuted, while investigators found no signs of injury or foul play.

The death was ruled accidental.

title: US must return to interim deal, no ceasefire extension talks, senior Iranian source says
description: There have been no talks on extending a ceasefire between Iran and the U.S. under an interim deal, with Iran saying that Washington must return to the pact
fullText:
DUBAI, Aug 12 (Reuters) - There have been no talks on extending a ceasefire between Iran and the U.S. under an interim deal, with Iran saying that Washington ‌must return to the pact and define a timeframe to implement its commitments, a senior ‌Iranian source told Reuters on Wednesday.

The source's comments came after Turkey's Anadolu news agency, citing Pakistani government sources, reported that ​Tehran and Washington had agreed to extend a 60-day ceasefire under their Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).

"One of the issues that is being discussed via mediators is the U.S. returning to the interim agreement and defining a timeframe for implementing its commitments. There has been absolutely no progress on this issue," the source said.

The interim deal ‌signed in June between Tehran and ⁠Washington declared an "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts", but quickly unravelled, with U.S. President Donald Trump saying on July 7 that the ⁠pact was "over". Tehran has repeatedly accused Washington of consistently violating its commitments.

"There is no talk of an extension because ... the United States violated the interim agreement 48 hours after it was reached and withdrew from it a ​few ​days later," the source told Reuters.

In the agreement, the ​60-day period refers to an extendable timeframe ‌within which Iran and the U.S. were expected to reach a final deal, which would include larger issues including the fate of Iran's disputed nuclear program.

A series of requirements, such as a ceasefire in Lebanon, free navigation in the Gulf and waivers for Iran to sell its oil, were viewed as necessary before entering the further negotiation period.

However, efforts to secure a lasting peace have hit an impasse over ‌a range of issues, including disagreements over the Strait ​of Hormuz.

Tehran says the vital shipping route will remain closed ​as long as the U.S. does not change ​its behaviour and accept Iran's conditions to end the war, including the unfreezing ‌of Iranian funds overseas.

After the start of ​the war, which began with ​U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, Tehran effectively shut the strait, through which a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas was shipped.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said ​on Sunday that Iran and the ‌U.S. are not engaged in talks and Tehran will not start them as long ​as Washington breaches the interim deal, adding that messages are being exchanged via intermediaries ​Pakistan and Qatar.

(Writing by Parisa HafeziEditing by Keith Weir)

title: Blanche, newly confirmed as AG, says 'Anti-Weaponization Fund' still dead
description: But he said there may be other ways of compensating "weaponization" victims.
fullText:
In his first news conference since his narrow confirmation as attorney general, Todd Blanche reiterated Wednesday that the Justice Department's "Anti-Weaponization Fund" will not be revived -- but suggested there could be other ways of compensating so-called "victims" of "weaponization."

Blanche's comments, during a press conference on an unrelated criminal fraud matter, came after President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office earlier this week that the Anti-Weaponization Fund's future would be Blanche's to decide.

The $1.776 billion fund was announced in May by the Justice Department to compensate those who allege they were wrongly targeted under the Biden administration. Blanche affirmed in a written order prior to his confirmation as attorney general that the fund was dead, under pressure from two Republican senators whose support for his nomination hinged on whether he would make such a declaration.

Key Republicans say they'll support Blanche for AG after he rescinds 'Anti-Weaponization Fund'

"I keep on saying this over and over again, but I'm happy to say it one more time," Blanche said at Wednesday's press conference in response to a question from ABC News. "I have testified under oath that it's dead. I have testified in front of the House where I wasn't under oath where I said it was dead. I have answered questions after my hearing where I said that it was dead, I have rescinded the order that that set up the weaponization fund, which means that it does not exist."

"I'm not sure how I can further say that the anti-weaponization fund doesn't exist, or we use the word 'dead,'" he added. "But if anybody has any ideas, we also have said under oath that if Congress would like to make it a law, that we would support that, as would the White House."

At the same time, Blanche suggested the department would entertain other means to pay out so-called "victims" of "weaponization" under the Biden administration, as President Trump has repeatedly said he wants.

"The president feels very strongly, as do I, that there were people who were victims of a Department of Justice that was absolutely weaponized, and he feels very strongly that that he would want to -- to make them whole, as do I, but it will not be through the Anti-Weaponization Fund," Blanche said.

The fund was proposed in exchange for Trump agreeing to drop his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS as well as two civil claims for $230 million related to the Russia collusion investigation he faced during his first term in office and the 2022 search of his Mar-a-Lago estate -- sparking accusations by critics of self-dealing and a bipartisan uproar over the possible use of taxpayer money to pay rioters who attacked the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.
